I have been on a retainer with one of the UK’s largest magazine companies for the last four years and as part of that agreement with them I have needed to bite my tongue and keep the peace. Well as of a few months ago the company is no longer a carphone warehouse client and I’m no longer bound so now I can let the fur fly ! and warn others considering moving their business account to carphone warehouse to think twice you’ll regret it if you put your account with them, they are incapable of upholding the promises made by their sales persons.

I have been in the communications industry for nearly thirty years and managed many mobile phone providers and virtual networks for the companies I have contracted for and in all that time I have never come across a company that displays such arrogance and lack of understanding of their own industry. I have also never felt so strongly to wright such a review to enlighten others to what they might be letting themselves in for.

Communications is carphone warehouse’s core business however they are so poor at communication it is no wonder that so many problems existed for the entirety of the account. The main office is in Poole Dorset and seemingly headed up by disillusioned people with thick skins who probably pat themselves on the back believing they are doing a good job. They truly have no idea how to run an office much less manage accounts. The operations director will pay lip service and come across as someone who wants to resolve problems but the reality is he is as ineffective as everyone else, worse if you try and make contact with head office he seems to be able to intercept that communication and you’ll end up having to deal with them again. We found it impossible to make contact with anyone outside that office.

One example of the problems were, one day we suddenly had a large number of mobiles that couldn’t make or receive calls. Having called them to report was told that it needed to be emailed into the account manager. They wouldn’t hear that it was urgent and people needed their mobiles working. A day later having been already given the mobile numbers effected in that email they wanted to know the numbers effected, DUH! Didn’t they read the email. They also wanted to know the postcodes of where every handset was when it couldn’t make a call. Sort of seems a reasonable question but they asked at 5pm on day two nearly twenty hours after the first report and when the email came back on day three at midday all we were told was that they thought all the sims were faulty and should be replaced and was that what we wanted them to organise? Again duh! They are meant to know what to do, we are the customer.

Not being satisfied with their suggestion, also beginning to lose the will to deal with them any more and frankly now looking incompetent to my employer because its gone on for so long without any proper diagnosis or even a sensible approach being adopted, I called network directly and reported the problem. It turned out that all the numbers effected had been blacklisted. All were un-blacklisted within a few minutes and all were again working within the hour, even through we were told it could take up to 24 hours.

After an investigation it turned out someone at carphone warehouse had make a mistake and emailed in the wrong list of IMEI’s. When challenged directly their initial excuse was they were acting on instructions from someone within the company, and when asked for the proof which they couldn’t provide they reluctantly owned up to the cockup in their office. We never did get a proper apology nor did we get an answer as to why someone had collated our IMEI’s together.

On another occasion we had a large number staff attend a conference in Europe. When they landed at Madrid none of their handsets worked. Two days without a working mobile amongst them and that turned out to be roaming wasn’t enabled. Despite their service manager stating several times in email that roaming is on by default and what ever the problem is it wont be that!. In desperation again we contacted the airtime provider and they resolved the matter quickly. In the mean time carphone wanted to replace the sims, we lost count over the course of the contract how many times they used that excuse for a break down in service, it seems to be their go-to solution, probably because it buys them time to allow a problem to fix its self or at least appears that something is being done. We never had a problem in the term of the contract that required a sim replacement to resolve.

These are just two of the dozens of examples of problems with them and their service, most of the other problems relate to slowness of what they call service, delayed responses and when they finally do respond if you don’t have to keep onto them it is usually to confirm information they have already been provided. Eventually we stopped contacting them and dealt directly with the airtime provider who was more than happy to help and always resolved matters quickly. Carphone warehouse probably thought everything was fine and had no idea that they had in effect been cut from the process.

It seemed as though they buy time with every email because they have no idea what to do. The attention span is short and the attention to detail is even shorter!. Efficient is not a word within their vocabulary. It is quite clear the general bar is low and the management bar is even lower.

So the bottom line is, avoid them and save your self a lot of time and inconvenience. The deal they do might be amongst the lowest you will receive and for us it was very competitive however in the long run it will cost you time and annoyance and you will end up managing them and your account your self so you might as well do a deal direct with the airtime provider and cut out the circus clowns at carphone warehouse.

Every negative review you will read online about carphone warehouse business is well deserved in our experience.

I’m now with another company and for a short while carphone warehouse was being considered, 350 mobiles very nearly transferred to their control. Thank god I got there in time.

Clueless warehouse was the nickname we gave to them and they earnt it too !

I must say, initially I was quite pleased with PC Specialist, but decided to hold off leaving a review until I'd used the PC for a while. Now, faults happen, and I don't think any company should be marked down for that; it's the way they respond that's important. Sadly, it has been a terrible experience, especially for a PC that cost over £6,000. A few faults occurred (the most important being only half the RAM started being detected), so a return was arranged. It's quite a significant process because the PC is large and must be returned on a full wooden forklift pallet. These are too large to fit through a UK front door, so the pallet and PC needs to be assembled outside (secured and then wrapped). Having done all this on the day of collection, no one arrived, so I had to dismantle it all and bring it back inside. I called PCS and they could provide no information whatsoever, and said "all couriers are having a delay, so we can't promise when it will be collected, but hopefully in the next day or so". Even when I protested and said I can't just have them randomly turn up because it's a pallet collection, I was told there was nothing they could do, and they couldn't get a better date from the courier (Palletways). If that was true, I wouldn't hold it it against them neccessarily - but it simply was false. I called Palletways directly (which isn't easy because its business-to-business) who were fantastic. They explained the collection was never due when PCS said, and it was scheduled for the following day, and they would have the driver call me. So extra marks to Palletways (who got a glowing review left for them). This was just laziness on the part of PCS - they could have done better here and simply chose not to do so (or have not trained their staff sufficiently).

The problems didn't end there - my PC has now been sat in a warehouse for the entire week because there are no technicians to actually look at it. Of course, it was exactly the same story again in that they could not tell me when it would be looked at "but hopefully we will get it back to you in a couple of weeks". I simply cannot believe they collected it, knowing they had no one available for weeks. And again, absolutely nothing this person on the phone could do - he couldn't even arrange a manager to call me back.

Since these problems occurred within 30 days of receiving it, I'm entitled to reject the goods for a full refund. I've explained by phone, and now email, that I'll be exercising this right tomorrow if I don't hear anything. And sadly, I'm fully expecting I will need to do that, as it'll be far quicker for me to reject the goods, and just buy a new PC from one of their competitors.

By contrast, last year my two-year-old Alienware PC started having an issue where the 2080 GPU fans would spin up to max, turning on and off. When I called Dell, they sent out a technician to home two days later, who not only swapped the GPU out with a new one, but also swapped the second GPU out too "just in case". Totally fixed the hardware issue within 3 days on a two-year-old system, completely free under warranty. I just looked now, and a very similar spec machine from Alienware costs £4799 (in fact, exactly the same spec, just not fully water-cooled - AIO, and slightly slower RAM clock). And it's fairly easy to get Dell to knock 15% off via live chat. My PCS build was £6300, yet this is the level of service. I'm fine paying more because that's the nature of a complete custom build - but the support needs to back it up for this price.

Overall, very disappointing - I went with PCS because they came highly recommended by a friend who purchased from them two years ago. When I explained this to him, his words were "wow, they have changed a lot. I remember I could even speak directly with the guy who build my PC. Maybe I won't get my next PC from them". The only reason I gave two stars here instead of one is because all the people on the phone are always incredibly nice, but they're just not empowered by leadership to do anything or escalate issues. If I were a manager here, I'd want to know someone is about to use their legal rights to have a 6 grand refund issued and maybe step in to get things on the right track. The mind boggles.

UPDATE: Shortly after posting this, I received a phone call from a chap called Marcus who was extremely helpful and apologetic, and laser focused on getting this issue sorted out. I think he went quite above and beyond in terms of the fact that before calling me, he went and checked the stock levels of the main components in my system to make sure he could be more confident around timelines. I've added a star on to the review, as a good measure of a company is how they put things right, and I could not fault the customer-recovery. It was refreshing that both Vodafone and Hyde Park Corner Ltd were open and honest about what had happened.
I feel fortunate my car was not stolen during this seven month period, as my insurance states I must have a tracker fitted and working.
I'm posting this review hoping that it reaches other customers of these two businesses detailing my experience. If it is later than the installation date then you have also been exposed to the invalidated insurance like myself.
Vodafone and Hyde Park Corner Ltd now say this problem has been rectified, and I can verify my Tracker now works correctly. My mistake was not to test the Tracker worked on installation, and trusting the two businesses involved to provide the service I had subscribed to.

I appreciate that RAM compatibility is tricky and sometimes there might be margin of error with certain models or systems. I have received two RAM modules (original order and replacement) stated as compatible with a HP Microserver Gen10 and neither will POST in this system.

There's always a small chance of having faulty RAM, which is why I accepted a replacement the first time, but it appears the same type of RAM module was shipped as a replacement, which leads me to believe this RAM generally is not going to work in this system (despite compatibility assurances), given two different sticks of the same RAM have been tried and won't work, unless an entire RAM batch is faulty, which is probably unlikely.

I've tried all the usual sanity/troubleshooting steps but I can't think of any other step to try other than the RAM itself being incompatible. The original 8GB HP RAM module that came with the system works fine in either of the two memory slots and can POST fine. I can say in good faith my installation and handling of the RAM received is not improper. I have tried both the original and replacement RAM in both memory banks and even with the original HP memory, which Windows Server seemed to recognise the RAM slot as having memory in, but it was not addressable or recognised in the BIOS.

The system will simply refuse to POST with any of the provided Integral RAM modules in the system. I can't get a display output and the fan continuously remains at a high RPM, suggesting the system is not booting.

I have unfortunately had to request a refund, as I have to accept that the RAM provided by yourselves isn't suitable for this system.

I will however praise your staff for being responsive and quick to handle the returns/refund process. All aspects of communication regarding my order have been fast and professional. It is just a shame that there appears to be a product incompatibility here.

If you do happen to have a HP Microserver Gen10 system and the Integral RAM that has been shipped as an upgrade can be demonstrated to POST in this system, I will happily amend this review and accept responsibility on my part.

Edit: I appreciate the response re: testing of RAM before shipping. I don't dispute that, this is however different to the RAM itself working in the system it is advertised as a compatible upgrade for. If the system won't POST then I'd have to dispute the "compatibility guarantee". It is likely the RAM shipped does work fine, but won't in this system.

Edit 2: I ended up sourcing some equivalent DDR4 ECC RAM from Crucial/Micron next business day at a slightly lower cost and it worked fine as soon as it was installed. I'm afraid I have to still maintain the RAM upgrade product you are providing for the HP Microserver Gen10 is not suitable.

Obviously (as I now know) that’s not what happened because for some ridiculous reason, in 2019 you can’t transfer numbers between contracts on the same network. You have to get a pay and go SIM on a new network, port your number across there, and then after 30 days, port it back - I can’t be without my existing phone number for 30 days, and nor should I have to pay for a new pay and go sim. I wasn’t told any of this at point of sale (and had no reason to already know about the number transfer, as I’ve always just upgraded rather than opened a new contract) so Carphone Warehouse completely mid-sold this to me. I will be returning the phone within the 14 days cooling off period and will upgrade directly with EE.

If you do decide to go with Carphone Warehouse, make sure you ask loads of questions and fully understand what they are doing. I suspect opening a new contract was probably only beneficial to the sales representative, who probably only gets commission for “new” contracts rather than upgrades. Particularly since they matched what EE were offering me in an upgrade - it wasn’t a better deal than I could get via upgrade.

I would not recommend this company. I’ve been a Vodafone customer for over 20 years on “pay as you go”. The actual phone service is fine but don’t try upgrading your phone. I received a text from them suggesting I upgrade to a 5g phone. The local Vodafone shop closed a couple of years ago but recently reopened. Drop in to the shop, buy a phone, get the staff to help transfer the sim etc. What could be simpler ? Before visiting the shop I checked the website to confirm what phones were available in my price range. However, the phone I wanted was not in stock and nor were several similar ones. Staff said they are not allowed to order in payg phones. “No problem”, I said – “there’s a sign in the shop saying Click & Collect, so I’ll just go on line and do that.” “Sorry”, they said, “we are not able to do Click & Collect anymore.” The staff were as helpful as they could be in the circumstances. They checked the website to confirm what was available for immediate delivery. They recommended two phones of similar spec to the one I originally asked for, available for payg customers.
I went home and ordered a phone on-line on Dec 7th. I received an email confirming my order and stating delivery would be between 8am and 6pm next day. My bank statement showed a pending transaction. I stayed in all day but nothing arrived. At 5:45 I received a text saying that due to “a technical issue” they could not provide the phone and asking me to go on the website for a chat. After much typing I spoke to a person who said the order had been cancelled. “Not by me”, I said. They said I should try again in a day or so. I repeated the process a day or two later. Same result, only this time without the courtesy of a text. After more web chat and a chat with a human I was given the phone number of the sales department. “They will be able to place the order for you”, they said. Sales dept said they could not place the order and recommended that I call in to my local Vodafone shop. At that point I should have given up but, ever the optimist, I placed an order on line again. I got a confirmation but no phone arrived. I gave up in frustration.
Throughout the webchats and phone calls I was asked several times if I would take out a contract. As soon as I said “no” the options seemed to be limited. I will be looking for another mobile phone provider asap. The only positive I can take from this is that the staff in the shop were polite and as helpful as they could be, given the constraints under which they have to operate. No transactions went through on my bank account so I am not out of pocket, only my time was wasted. My advice to Vodafone is not to offer for sale products you cannot provide and to ensure your staff know what the different departments can and cannot do. Give your shop staff greater authority to meet the needs of all your customers.

They purposely try and undersell you. Out of the 9+ phones my family have sent to them, every single attempt has tried to claim the ‘battery health’ was too low if there’s nothing else they can mark it down on. That tends to be their go to, as there’s no way to prove it once the device is out your hands, so most just accept it and move on.

(For context: both of the BEST options for sale require a minimum of 80% battery health, anything under that is classed under their faulty segment. Which can take a £150 sale to something more like £50 in a matter of seconds.)

Before shipping off, ALWAYS check your battery health yourself before tricking yourself into believing them. (For iPhone users, this is as simple as checking in your settings.) Plus, take photos to prove the original condition of things, as scratches can sometimes be used too. (Preferably, take a video that also shows you packing it too, if you wanted added security.)

If they try claim it’s lower for any reason when you’ve ensured so yourself, refuse the deal and request it to be shipped back. 9/10 times, they will reply back with an attempt to keep your consumer. Their emails usually go on about a fictional ‘further review’ so they’ll amended the price to something FAR closer to the original quote. But still not as much as it should be.)

Other than that, make sure you read the conditions for each of the 3 classifications carefully, and memorise exactly what your phone falls in.

I wish I had never bought the Canon Pixma TS6350A.
It had splendiferous reviews and was a 'good buy' on the Which website and the print quality is better than my old Canon printer.
So, it took me 3 hours to set it up (and I used to work in IT so I am IT savvy).
The advice I can give is (to Mac users):-
1. Delete your existing printer first via 'Settings'.
2. It requires you to enter your wifi password and the intuitive thing is to press the 'OK' button after each character but actually you need to press the green downward triangle not the OK button.
3. The biggest fault this printer has is - it has TWO paper feeders. There is one at the bottom front of the printer and another at the top back of the printer. Put paper in both of them to set it up. I didn't and it took an hour to work this out.
4. The print quality is good. However, if you are printing from a variety of sources e.g. Word, Excel, the web, photos, you HAVE to put the paper into BOTH feeders as only a few of these sources allow you to choose which paper feeder to use.
5. The bottom feeder needs photo paper putting in facing away from you (the bottom feeder is called 'the cassette'). The top paper feeder needs photo paper putting in facing you.
6. The output of printed sheets automatically juts out when you try to print something. I got spurious errors when I pulled it out in anticipation of printing something.
7. I could NOT load more than 2 sheets of photo paper without it issuing an error message. I could only load about 7 pages of normal printing paper before it issued an error message.

So, if you want good printing results and good ink usage then this is the printer for you. But if you don't want to waste your life on error messages and the wrong type of paper being used - look elsewhere. Argos were brilliant at fulfilling my order. Canon & Which let me down.

Some background - I have a rental flat where a family with 2 young kids reside. I have had the D&G boiler service contract for the best part of ~25 years and as the boiler has worked pretty much faultlessly, I have barely needed to use the contract during this period. It was currently costing £41 per month but at the start it cost around £11 - they have increased the price over the years.

On around the 23rd November, issues with the heating in the apartment coupled with the front cover of the boiler getting very hot started. I called Potterton who eventually put me through to Baxi and an engineers visit was scheduled for the Monday 28th November.

Baxi came round on the Monday and said new replacement parts were needed and would call us back as to when they could get back to replace the parts. I asked them if we would just be better at this stage replacing the boiler as it was ~25 years old now and although it made sense practically they said unless D&G give the go ahead they can't write it off.

By this time temperatures were starting to fall with the cold snap coming in.

Baxi called back and said the earliest they could get someone round was the 5th December.

My tenant was doing their best to get through this by using the immersion heater in combination with electric heaters.

The Baxi engineer came round on the 5th and replaced the parts but left us with a 'Warning Notice' stating that the boiler should not be used.

I called Baxi to better understand what was going on - I was told there was an issue with the flu which was not covered by the service contract. They also said I needed to get a '3rd' part to asses the boiler - I have no idea what they meant by this.

I got a 2nd opinion from a qualified boiler engineer who confirmed that the best course was to replace the boiler.

What made it so frustrating was that even Baxi acknowledged that the cost of trying to repair the boiler would be more than what D&G would have to contribute for a replacement boiler but they still could not write the boiler off.

By now we had wasted nearly 3 weeks where the boiler should have just been green lighted for replacement after the 1st visit. It was coming up to Xmas and with the cold weather we did not have the luxury of wasting further time so I started the process of getting a new boiler fitted.

A new Valiant boiler was fitted before Xmas and thankfully that is working now.

Had D&G accepted that a new boiler was needed, they would have to pay I think £750 - the call outs alone and the spare parts had cost more than that. We could have had a new boiler fitted within 10 days and then the family would not have had to manage through the cold snap.

The new boiler comes with a 10 years parts guarantee.

My experience has made it clear - for boilers these insurance service contracts are a waste of money - don't be drawn into them. If your boiler breaks down use google to find a good engineer and in 99.9% of cases it will always cost you less than forking out on these agreements.

Would give no stars if possible.

When I tried to move house with BT, they initially told me they could only give me a much slower speed at the new flat, so said I could leave my contract at no cost. However, instead of cancelling on the spot, they recommended I check what I could get elsewhere, as they claimed nobody else would be able to offer me a better speed anyway, so I may as well stick with them. If someone else could, they said, I could just ring back and cancel at no cost.

So I did, like a fool.

Finding out Hyperoptic could give me a much faster connection and had a limited time offer on I could take advantage of right now, I signed up for them, and thought I could then just ring BT to cancel like they'd said I could, like a fool.

When I then rung back and tried to cancel BT, they said actually I'd have to pay about £240 to cancel. I explained the last person had said I could cancel no fee, and I wanted to hold them to that, but they held steady. Eventually, with no real way to pay a £240 fine even if I could eventually argue that I should get it back, I gave up and said I'd book in a move with them, thinking that would at least just leave me paying the same as before, like a fool.

Hyperoptic were very nice about letting me cancel when I explained the mix-up, and agreed to let me keep my service with them until the date I'd booked for the BT house move, and the let me use the introductory rate they'd offered even though I was pulling out of the contract that was meant to commit me to. I think they felt sorry for how badly BT had treated me. So I organised with them to end my service on the day the BT would start, like a fool.

Of course, the BT never started. Nobody turned up at the house and nothing went live. When I rang up, they said they had no record of my having talked to them about moving home (which, by this point, I'd done about 5 times). Also, apparently the service at the old place was still going and being charged (they said they'd cancel it from when I booked the move).

By this point I had no internet at all, and no prospect of any for a few weeks. But the best they could do was book me in another installation and definitely cancel my old contract this time. I thought about just giving up at this point, going back to Hyperoptic, and taking the £240 fine. But I thought BT would at least arrange the move right this time, like a fool.

Several weeks of no internet later, the 2nd installation date came and went with no engineer and nothing going live. Again when I rang up it was like I was asking to move home for the very first time. No record of anything. And service still going at my old place and still being charged.

Worse, when I got a bill through, it turned out they'd moved me to a much more expensive contract, back-dated that to the date of our very first conversation about a home move, and removed a loyalty discount I'd previously had, and backdated that removal, and signed me up for BT Sport, and backdated that! The amount of money that went out on that direct debit was mind-bending!

I then sort of lose track of it in my memory. I struggled on without internet for weeks, racking up bills on my 4G contract like nobody's business. I was job-hunting at the time and the lack of home internet was crippling. At one point, another bafflingly inflated bill full of stuff I'd never asked for and confusing additions and removals of odd amounts of money arrived an hour before a job interview, and I unwisely called up about it and had a stressful and unpleasant conversation, and got so upset a friend had to intervene, convince me to just drop it for now, and focus on the job interview (which I did not perform well in).

It got to the point, even after the internet eventually started in the new place, that every time a bill came through I would suffer anxiety and delay opening it for days, fearful of what nonsense might be in it. They kept on charging me for random stuff, for months after they got the internet started up, and I kept having to call up and talk about it. I ended up in tears on several occasions. The whole experience gave me a fear of talking to companies on the phone about utility stuff that took ages to properly shake, and indirectly caused several more issues where I didn't raise problems or complain about things that were wrong because I was so scared of something like this happening.

Somehow this all led to me getting locked into a 18-month contract at the new place, and once, months after the move, it was all finally humming along, they offered me a year of free BT Sport to say sorry, and I felt stupid turning it down even though it filled me with trepidation, so I took it, and of course at the end of that it took 3 tries over 3 months to cancel it. When I eventually left and moved back to Hyperoptic, it took months for me to even feel up to writing this review.

It is very clear that the staff at New Street were being as obstructive as possible so that I would feel compelled to buy a new phone. I will never trust this company again. Condition of the phone:

When I opened the box the first thing I noticed QMF didn't include a screen protector and headphones even though I paid for the full bundle and it should have been there. When I took the phone I saw some deep scratches on the stainless steel at the bottom left corner. When I turned the phone around I found a small crack at the back of the phone. Again I bought the phone in pristine condition... I switched on the phone and set it up. When the phone was on I noticed that the bezels around the screen seemed to be thicker than on the original screen. I went to the settings and there was no option of true tone (which means that the part was replaced and it wasn't original). I also tried 3d touch which didn't work either. I went to youtube to check the speakers, they were of good quality however on the maximum volume I could hear some distortions of the sound.

The refund process

I contacted QMF and claimed the refund the same day, they sent me the labels for sending the phone back and I did it the same day. They received the phone on 20.04.2020 and on 21.04.2020 they processed it for the refund. They didn't send me the email confirming the refund (it is very important! I wiil talk about it later). I contacted them in online chatbox and they told me that the refund takes 14 working days, so they should have given the money back to DivideBuy by 11.05.2020. However, surprise surprise it didn't happen. I contacted DivideBuy and they asked me to send them an email which confirms that QMF confirmed the refund. I emailed QMF and cc DivideBuy in the conversation and they never replied to this email. Fortunately, I took the screenshots of the conversation and sent them to DivideBuy, so they stepped in and wrote QMF directly. QMF promised them to process the refund by 18.05.2020, yet it didn't happen either.I wrote to DivideBuy one more time and they contacted QMF again. Hence on 19.05.2020, I got an email from QMF that my refund was processed and today on 21.05.2020 I got my money back from the DIvideBuy. I am not sure if I could get money back if I paid QMF directly, DivideBuy helped me a lot in this process. If I were you I wouldn't buy any phone from them, It is my story, hope it helps. I gave 2 stars which is very generous from my side. QMF thank you for giving my money back.

I have been a customer with 3 for 17 years and my recent experience with them has left me frustrated, confused and at a complete loss as to where I can find resolution, without resorting to another convoluted process, writing in to complain to them.

Of course, it has to do with requesting a refund they are refusing to give. Not because I'm not owed it but because no one seems to have the authority to action it.

Here's my story:
Instead of just cancelling my contract, an old tariff that ran out years ago, and putting me on an alternative, by looking at my usage, pitched against what I currently pay, 3 decided to put me on a much more expensive tariff, without any consultation with me. Each call to the Indian call centres, resulted in me having to deal with a different customer service rep, who kept trying to sell me new deals, without first trying to resolve the problem I had. They even seemed to suggest that, were I to take one of their new deals, we could resolve the refund problem. In retrospect I realise how much this sounds like blackmail. So many hours were spent on the phone to them, achieving little. Later I was told, on the one call I managed to talk to a manager, the clock and not been turned back on on my tariff, that it was not possible, even though the 3 app was telling me it had been done. 

When you push the customer service reps to address the issue, as they try to sell you new deals, they continually tell you "I'm not authorised to do that". When you ask for someone in a higher position, that may be authorised, or able to help you further, they say a manager will call you but "will probably not tell you anything more than I'm telling you". I had two call backs from line managers where I just missed getting to the phone, only to receive a voicemail telling me to call them back, which forced me to go back, yet again, to the customer call centre to have the same conversation over and over again with yet another lower level customer service rep. 

The third call from a manager, not only contradicted the second call centre rep, on the roll back, but he pretty much said there was nothing he could do, as he was not "authorised to do so". It was a mantra everyone I spoke to said. Clearly 3 have put into place a system where NO-ONE is "authorised" to action a refund.

I know it already sounds confusing but I've tried not to give more detail because it would convoluted, boring, and even more confusing. Safe to say, I've been sent round in circle after circle, with call centre staff misinforming me, and contradicting each other, whilst telling me 'they know exactly how I feel, and how they would feel the same, under the same circumstances, but that they are "not authorised to" reverse the charge'. After a week of this, it actually made me ill.

In 17 years, 3 have never been the best phone service, just the cheapest. Now they feel like crooks. I am left feeling that even if I write in to complain, little or nothing, will be resolved. They will simply keep the extra money they decided I should pay without my consultation. I can't even leave and find a better deal for a month, as I'm tied in to the expensive rolling contract for this first month. 

It's criminal for anyone to take money from others when they've not agreed to it. It's theft when you ask for it back and they refuse to return it, or make it so difficult, you are just forced to give up. 

I'm dreading going through the complaints process. But will. I'm hoping to complain to the Ombudsmen, after all they have put me through.

After a much better than expected experience with Shell energy something occurred that was to severely tarnish our judgement of the company.
Back in mid December, after much badgering by Shell, we caved in and had our old meters changed to smart ones. The new meters worked absolutely fine... but our online account usage data graphs for the old meters completely disappeared (this included the downloadable CSV files that I could use in Excel). This meant that our careful energy usage cutbacks, which we could compare to the last year using the online graphs, were not viewable. I would have to resort to use the old bills data and calculate the individual months usage to compare how well we were doing and not rely on seeing it easily in a visual graphic manner online. I just wanted at the 'old' CSV files at the very least as they would enable me to 'recreate' the 'old' graphs.
I contacted, by phone, a customer representative. I was told that it would be looked into and someone would contact me. This did not happen.
I contacted again and again but no answer to the problem but more promises of a call back.
After eventually being told that there was no way to show the 'old' meter readings alongside the 'smart' meter readings on a graph, I asked if, at least, I could have the CSV files of the historical data, I was finally passed to 'resolutions' but again the promised call-back from the 'case handler' did not happen.
This happened a few more times.
But eventually, nearly a month after beginning the 'enquiry' a person, Graeme, from Complaints resolution actually contacted me and was a very knowledgeable guy indeed.
Graeme sorted out everything (there were a couple of other issues that had cropped up (post meter installation) in an excellent manner. He also enabled our dumping of the 'Economy 7' tariff as it was no longer economical for us ( after January's increase in the E7 unit tariffs) .

So all is well in the end and our faith in the Shell has been restored... so far....
BUT if you are going to change to smart meter(s) and you use the online graphs or CSV files for your easy usage graphical comparison to historical year(s) before, then take a screen shot of the graphs and download the CSV files before the day of meter changeover so that you can continue to easily visually track your efforts in cutting back on energy by comparing your new 'smart meter' graphs to your old data.

I've been with NOW TV for over a year and was - until recently - reasonably happy with their service (reliability, cost, speed). Having moved house, I decided to re-contract with them, and scheduled an engineer visit for the activation of my broadband line.

The engineer visited on the 31st of August, but because he didn't complete the work, the service did not go live. In the following days, during which there was a complete lack of communication from NOW TV, I decided to call the customer line to arrange for a new appointment. To my surprise, instead of prioritizing customers who have already been delayed, they explained to me that I would have to make-do with an appointment in 14 days at the earliest, because new customers take priority.

Fast forward 10 days, when I received an email that my second appointment had been cancelled. To add insult to injury, the email asked that I offer 3 weekdays for the next appointment (this time starting "only" 10 days in the future) . I received no response to my request for being allocated a single appointment date (as opposed to 3), considering their poor service record.

Finally, 18 days after the line was meant to go live, I called their service line again, where I found out that my order had been cancelled in its entirety without notice, because NOW TV had not received their 3 weekdays. I suspect that this is largely a strategy to weasel out of paying me the large sum in auto-compensation that I have accumulated.

Following their egregious conduct, I will be taking my business elsewhere and can only advise that you do the same.

On this X1, the existing battery slides out forwards. Remove the pinned battery covers, then the 4 bolted square bar that crosses the engine bay and 2 bolts (16mm ish) that hold a battery front cover in place which slides upwards. The batt retention metal plate can then be accessed and lifted off - one bolt here (13mm ish). Remove pinch bolt on terminal block so cable can be parted. After many questions to, I assume, verify it was me who purchased the phone, 1 question at a time. Rather than just ask, 'hey can you verify the model, colour and method of purchase' I was asked each question at a time, which in a chat draws out the process ridiculously. Ordered (online) a Sim-free phone from CPW on Thurs 25 June. Changed my mind the following morning as current network provider offered me a much better deal. I rang CPW on the morning of Fri 26 June to cancel order, and was advised that if refused the DPD delivery at the doorstep then the phone would be returned to CPW and I would receive a refund back to my account within 3-5 working days. DPD's tracking shows the phone being delivered back to CPW on Monday 29 June. A week later, there was no sign of my refund, so I went on to the online chat on CPW's website, where their staff told me that the refund would come to me as a cheque in the post, and would take 14-28 days. When I questioned why this had changed and why it couldn't be refunded back to the original method of payment (Visa debit card), CPW said they didn't hold any bank account details for me. This is complete nonsense... If CPW are able to take a Visa payment, their merchant management system should allow them to issue a refund back to the card regardless of whether CPW have 'stored' any account details.

Having chased CPW up a few times, and been given different information each time by Customer Service, I eventually received a cheque in the post today (23 July), 10 days later than stated in The Consumer Contracts Regs 2013, of which Part 3 Section 34 states...
(4) Reimbursement must be without undue delay, and in any event not later than the time specified in paragraph (5) or (6).
(5) If the contract is a sales contract and the trader has not offered to collect the goods, the time is the end of 14 days after—
(a)the day on which the trader receives the goods back, or
(b)if earlier, the day on which the consumer supplies evidence of having sent the goods back.

Indeed I would have been ok with the delay if they were up-front about it and gave a reason, but the contradictory misinformation they gave only serves to annoy customers.

I won't be buying from CPW again because:
1) I don't like being lied to;
2) I don't deal with companies that flout basic consumer protection laws and openly acknowledge it.

I'm sure CPW will have some excuse about it being due to Coronavirus or whatever, although it doesn't appear to affect the speed at which they take your money, only refunding it.

My advice to anyone buying from CPW would be to pay on a credit-card and if you return goods for a refund and CPW are 'sticky' about giving you your money back, contact your card provider to request it via Chargeback.

As a company I feel that CPW’s time has passed, and doubt it will be too long before their contracts with other network providers go the same way as O2's, simply because they offer nothing of value to the consumer; indeed they only serve as a frustrating to deal with link between operators and consumers... something that the operators can cut-out by bringing the retail aspect of their businesses entirely in-house.

Myself and my partner have recently purchased and moved into a fantastic new build flat in Bracknell. In setting up our new home, WiFi was one of the top priorities on our to do list, as I am sure is the same with most people now a days. We began our WiFi search with a trip to our local Carphone Warehouse store in Bracknell where we spoke to the Branch Manager - Nathaniel. He conducted a search on our property to show what providers were available for us, we were presented with TalkTalk, Sky, Shell and SSE. After comparing average guaranteed speeds and monthly costs etc. we decided to go with SSE. This was originally set up in my partner's name. After placing the order we got a letter on Monday 16th September from SSE saying that the credit check has been denied. Being concerned, I contacted SSE to understand why this was the case, after some investigation it was because the Bracknell Branch Manager had incorrectly inputted the address on the system (road name was included on first line of address). This has therefore left a denied credit mark on my partner's credit history of which we have worked very hard to keep as clean as possible. In a rush to try and get WiFi set up (as my partner works from home), I headed to the Bracknell Carphone Warehouse store again to re-set up in my name. Later that day, I contacted the Carphone Warehouse customers services to understand why this process has taken over a week to only be denied. The first 2 advisors I spoke to hung up on me and the third put me through to a completely different department after I was put on hold for 30 mins. By this time is was 19:55 and was told that someone may not necessarily come back to me today. I requested for a call back the following day. To note here, I spent over an hour and a half on the phone to Carphone Warehouse on Monday 16th. I got a call the next day and was offered £50 credit on my account to tie myself and my partner over until the new SSE WiFi order (in my name) is set up. She told me that the best option would be to purchase data sim from a Carphone Warehouse store and put this into my iPad so we can have more data.
In regards to my new WiFi order, I stayed in contact with SSE to ensure this would pass the credit in case of any further address errors and they confirmed a few days later that the order was being processed, credit check has passed and I should expect the WiFi to be set up in 10 working days. Please note: the SSE customer services manager was excellent and very helpful. However, this was not as simple as it should have been. I received a call the following day from SSE saying that they cannot provide WiFi to our address. I was confused at Carphone Warehouse's system, why it would give me SSE as a provider option if they cannot actually provide WiFi to my property?
This leads me on my next adventure, to try to get some data for my iPad to use in our property, I headed to the Bracknell store to purchase the data sim (as instructed by customer services using the £50 in my customer account). Unfortunately I was told that as this is a new store and do not stock these sim cards. The store suggested I walk down to the store based in Currys (also in Bracknell) to see if they had any in stock. I headed down but unfortunately was again told that they didn't have any available 'because they were a small store'. They suggested I head to Reading as the store there is bigger. So today, Sunday 22nd September, I went to the Reading store (approx. 20 mile round trip) to only be told that these data sim cards don't actually exist anymore and are not stocked at any store. They suggested I raise my concerns with the store back in Bracknell and the customer services team. After being sent on a wild goose chase, I went back to Bracknell and purchased a Vodafone MiFi product for £70 on a rolling contract as this was the closest product I could get to a data sim as we urgently needed data for my partner's work (in order to pay the mortgage on our new flat). After going through yet another credit check, I purchased this and off I went to set it up. Once I got home, as suggested by the store manager in Reading, I decided to log another complaint with Carphone Warehouse about the system error (showing me providers that don't actually supply to our property) and that I have been misinformed by customer services and the stores to send me running around after a product that doesn't exist. This has cost me time, multiple parking costs and fuel. I have to say, I am very disappointed with my experience today with the customer services department. I first tried to contact the team, I was told to 'press 1' for general enquiries etc. once I clicked this the automated voice said 'our website provides a lot of answers to any questions - goodbye'. A little confused, I called back to ensure I clicked the correct number and the same happened again. I then called back again and had to go through the purchasing department who surprisingly didn't send me to the website and they kindly transferred me to the customer services team. Once I got through, I spoke to a woman called Marche who I explained my previous complaint to and the more recent issues. She told me that as £50 had previously been given they couldn't give me the difference to the £70 I actually paid - which after a bit of backwards and forwards, I understood and accepted this. She also explained that the providers are responsible to provide the information about what addresses they can supply WiFi to - again, after a bit of backwards and forwards I also accepted this. This then let me onto the issue about my time spent running around to different stores but she told me that this is a broadband related issue and that she can't do anything. Of which I don't agree with as my issues simply relate to the stores and the information about a data sim given by customer services. She also said that because £50 has already been awarded that they cannot do anything else. I tried to explain that I am raising a new complaint however she was clearly reading from a script and I did not feel that she was listening to me at all. After multiple requests, I was put through to a manager and once again, explained the issue. He said that Carphone Warehouse do not compensate for time and I should have called up all the stores before to ask what they had in stock before visiting. I understand that there are many means to find out stock but when a customer services advisor tells me to visit a store - that is what I am going to do and I don't think I should be accountable for that. I do however hold Carphone Warehouse accountable for their customer services telling me to visit a store and then brushed off by multiple members of staff at the stores themselves. All of which, in my opinion, is due to a lack of knowledge and training. The manager on the other end of the phone, Shameem, said that 'Carphone Warehouse will not provide you with any compensation' and 'that you need to raise the complaint externally but I can't tell you how to do that'. I then questioned if compensation cannot be awarded, how could I haven been given £50 for my previous complaint, the response to this was 'because the previous advisor wanted to resolve your complaint' which I then asked 'are you telling me that yourself and Marche don't want to resolve my complaint?' which he surprisingly quickly changed his answer and backtracked. I was left in a situation where I have been refused to speak to Shameem's manager, cannot be told how to complain 'externally' and denied of any compensation of my time or money spent.

I am very disappointed by the customer service and information that has been supplied by Carphone Warehouse and I do hope that this can be correctly rectified.

I'm going to make this clear right now. Every phone call I made was met with the most helpful, patient, courteous and just generally nice people. You could sense their frustration at the delay and they tried their best to expedite, but they can only do so much. They really are a credit to the company and the company should hold onto them as it can't be brilliant doing their job with certain customers - give then a pay rise in line with inflation at least.
That said, here's the lowdown;
1 star deducted for the Admin taking 4 extra days above their average time to inject the key.
1 star deducted since I have to pay £19 to expedite delivery to fall on the weekend when the task could have been finished Tuesday/Wednesday.
I star deducted for them not updating their website with a caveat that advises people there will be a longer than usual wait due to the Admin being too busy or being a prima donna.
1 star added for the excellence in forward facing staff.
I think that's pretty fair.
Finally if you've read this far, I can't personally recommend due to my experience, but remember my experience may be far different from yours. I can only go on what I have found and would in no way seek to influence anyone.

I then contacted the chatbot to try and cancel my contract through there. Again, I was told that my date of birth did not match up so I would not be able to access support.

Frustrated, I phoned the support line AGAIN and this time, when giving my date of birth, it was accepted! I then asked the woman on the phone if I could end my contract by cancelling my direct debit with Three. She said that yes, I would be able to do this, and confirmed more than once that everything would be sorted on their side so that I would make no more payments. I thought that was it.

A few months later though, I received a message from PDCS stating that I owed £58.17 to Three and that this debt was now affecting my credit score. They continued to send me several messages weekly demanding that I pay Three now or further action would be taken.

Obviously stressed, I phoned Three for support and yet again was told that my date of birth did not match. When I told the man on the phone that I had no idea why this was the case because I KNOW I gave my correct DoB in store (not to mention my ID was scanned), he told me to seek help from the online chatbot instead.

I did this and was finally told that I could change my date of birth by sending some details to an email address. Apparently I would receive a response within 5 working days. This did not happen.

I sought help from the chatbot again to enquire about when I would receive a response to the email and was told that my date of birth had already been changed on the account (I just hadn’t been informed). From there, I finally asked for my contract to be cancelled once and for all… but was told that I would have to pay the outstanding payments first. When I explained that I had phoned Three months ago to ask whether my contract could be ended after cancelling my direct debit - and was told yes - the man told me that there was no record of that call ever taking place. I told him that it definitely had but it was heavily implied that the conversation never happened (i.e. I was lying). In the end, I paid the money I ‘owed’ because I couldn’t take the stress of it anymore.

Safe to say, the whole experience left me incredibly distressed, has affected my credit score and has (unfairly) left me out of pocket at a time where money is tight for most people.

One problem with using the internet for so much is that it needs to have enough bandwidth for several things at once! So we decided it was time to upgrade the internet. We went onto a popular Meerkat-fronted comparison site and settled on NowTV Broadband. They set a date of 21st May for a switch over.

We realised that, in for a penny in for a pound, it would make sense to upgrade to their super fast broadband. So we called on 15th May, a week after signing up, to ask if we could upgrade to an even faster package. We were told to ring back after the connection went live, to make the change.

The day of the connection change came and went with no switchover. The following morning we called again, to see what was happening. We were informed that it was being dealt with, that the change would happen in the next few hours. We were assured that our current connection wouldn’t be switched until after the new connection was ready.

A few hours later the internet and telephone lines cut out. We installed the new NowTV box and nothing happened.

We called back and were told that there was a problem. We were given no details on when it would be resolved, or what the actual issue was. We were told a manager would call us back at some point. The customer service agent couldn’t say when, simply gave a date 3 days later by which she ‘hoped’ a manager would be able to call us. They said the problem was showing as flagged on their system as being explained to us on 15th May. When asked if they could review the recordings of that call, they said they would not and refused to give them to us but admitted they existed.

We then called our previous provider and asked if there were any problems with them or with Openreach (the vague reasons for the problem we were given). An engineer assured us that there was and should be no problem.

No other contact from NowTV was received. No internet connection came online.

This morning we have called twice and both times have been given different information, which doesn’t match. We have been told that we will be called back multiple times, no calls have been forthcoming. They have refused to confirm these issues. When asked for information on how to check the fault with Openreach we were told to google the number and when it was explained that not having internet made this more difficult and asked for the number we were told that due to GDPR we could not be given a number, despite it being in the public domain.

We asked to make a formal complaint. We were told to go online.

Times are tough and they are obviously working under strain. Technical difficulties happen. The tone and support from NowTV has made it impossible to feel reassured that I will be able to work effectively. They indicate it could be up to 10 days before the fault is corrected. This is despite the two week period between signing up and the connection coming online. It has also been over a week since they claim (erroneously) we were informed.

Looking on NowTV’s own forums reveals that this exact issue has happened countless times before. Each time they have blamed other companies but been ultimately responsible. On occasions it has taken them more than 16 days to resolve the issue.

In the meantime, we are stuck with no broadband, no telephone line, and no clue when we will be able to even know when work can resume.

They have now said that they would escalate the problem to 'Tier 2' and call us within 72 hours. It has been over 100 hours since then. Still not a single call or email. No apology.

Not to worry, I get a text to say the 'case manager' will call me on the day and at the time that I had arranged. I get another missed call notification - right day, wrong time!

I wait an extra hour, just in case. No call. I call them to find out why I have not been called and after 20 minutes of listening to muzak, I get no real help. I hang up to discover the 'case manager' had called while I was on the phone to one of their 'service agents' - over an hour later than arranged and notified!

My last verbal interaction was to tell the 'case manager' to call me about my ongoing lack of internet connection by 6pm that evening or I would be done with Talktalk. No call.

I emailed a few times with questions and asking for suggestions, and got well informed and speedy replies each time. I was directed to a choice of cooling solutions matching what I wanted, they confirmed that the RAM in the system would be matching what I already owned right down to the SKU, and explained how PCS goes about their Overclocking process. In the end, I could customize my build which a wide variety of Brands and Components that it felt like ordering individual parts to my own preference, despite buying from an SI.

When I did place my order, I noticed a potential error regarding the fans that would come with my build (Case should have come with only 3, but it was displaying 4, which was a potential problem since it wouldn't let me add that extra fan in the configurator since it "already existed") so I contacted PCS again and the rep went to the warehouse just do double check for me. When he couldn't find the specific case I ordered to check it out, he put a note into my order to include the extra fan free of charge if it's not already in there. I even got a personal contact Email for a PCS Support Agent for any other concerns. Ordering was overall made incredibly easy.

Once the PC arrived, the packing was incredibly secure and the build quality was as phenomenal as the customer service. Cable Management is a 10/10, everything is routed cleanly and nicely organized behind the rear panel of the case. Even though I didn't buy a GPU with my build, PCS made sure to route my PCIE Power Cable into a position that I could just slip it into my GPU after I installed it myself.

Overall 10/10 service, highly recommend to anybody thinking about getting a PC in the UK.

First of all, let me make it clear that if I could have left a zero star review I would have done! Here is my story:

As they could not put us on another line, as suggested by the engineer, we decided to get our internet elsewhere via 4G, and just keep a basic landline with BT as we're very rural, and can't rely on a mobile signal or 4G in case of emergency. I even had an argument with a member of staff that I was speaking to on the phone at the time, when I told him that I'd just received an email telling me that my broadband AND phone line were to be cut off, when he'd just confirmed that ONLY my broadband was to go. I even read it out to him, but he said on his screen it clearly said that I was only going to lose my broadband. I asked him who I could speak to to get it sorted out, and he said he 'didn't know!' I was sick to the back teeth of BT by this point, and had even tried emailing their CEO TWICE with no response, so decided to try contacting them via Resolver. Finally, the next day I received a call from someone high up, who sorted everything out .......... or so we thought!! This was about a month ago, then today, I opened an email from BT, telling me that as I was now having my broadband back, I would no longer be receiving the discount for my line rental!!! Not only that, but we also discovered that our landline has been cut off this morning!! I have spoken to someone at BT who confirmed that the landline has been cut off, and it's not just a fault, and she is now looking into it!! Whether or not I'll get a call back remains to be seen.

Meanwhile, I am left wondering why a company as big as BT can't seem to get even the simplest task right, and would recommend anyone even thinking of using them to go elsewhere, or risk months and months of frustration, and wasted time on phone calls to people who just can't seem to do their job properly anymore.

I recently found out about Bark and decided to give it a try for my production company. The category I was given to use was “Professional Video Services”. I went in expecting something similar to Upwork, but it’s more comparable to Craigslist with a better UI. Over the course of two weeks I was inundated with requests to shoot birthday parties, funerals, sex tapes, edit Ring doorbell footage, and a handful of other simple requests that require anything but a professional. In total I saw over 100 “leads” like this. I was immediately disappointed in the lack of accountability with the leads. They aren’t required to specify a budget, or any other details really. I even got one lead that had an amazing pitch, which I discovered was a videographer trying to get companies like mine to spend their money on bogus leads. It worked.

I was thrilled when I discovered a couple of diamonds in the rough, so I purchased the leads. Bark’s system allows only 5 people to purchase a lead. Each of these had only 2 purchases, so 3 remained. Upon following up with the leads I was told they’d already hired someone. So… why is the lead still available for me to purchase? I called customer support to let them know there had been a mistake. Surely they’d give me those credits back to use on actual leads. The incredibly rude woman on the phone told me the mistake was in fact me, not them. She said the lead was more than 15 minutes old, so I shouldn’t have purchased it. WHAT!? Additionally she told me they have no system in place to remove leads once someone has been hired, so that was also my fault. They offered zero help or empathy. Figuring this was just a disgruntled employee, I emailed the managerial team after she begrudgingly gave me their email address. Their website boasts a 24 hour response time. I followed up twice before I finally heard back a week later. Their response? A generated email telling me they don’t offer refunds, with a link on “how to make the best of your Bark experience”.

Their system is probably good if you’re looking for someone to help out with some yard work, but it is absolutely no place for a professional video company to be. They should not be allowed to use those words on their platform. I’m in over $400 that I won’t get back and have nothing to show for. Learn from my mistake and steer clear.

Here is a summary of our experience using the Carphone Warehouse.

The order was placed on Saturday evening after around 9 failed attempts because the website said that the details being used did not match - even though they did, the bank has all our correct details etc.

We explained this to the agent and she said "oh....maybe three...or o2?" The agent then explained that there is nothing carphone warehouse can do to help us.

We asked to be transferred to a UK based call centre as the agent explained that remote working agents in other countries cannot help us, and we reached sales.

The young girl in sales (possibly Shereen?) was very polite and apologetic and explained that the order had failed due to security checks from the contract provider we were trying to buy from (ID) and said she will place the order manually. She did this, and the deposit of £50.01 was taken from our bank account - the deposit was supposed to be £49.99 but for the sake of 2 pennies, we let it slide. She explained she would speak to ID and then call us back. When she called back my partner was on the phone to the doctor, so we missed the call.

We called back, reached the remote call centre, and made it back to sales. We then spoke to Jay and explained the situation. He looked at the notes and said he could see what Shereen (?) had started, and he would finish it. He took some details, made some calls and said that the order was all successful and that the Phone would be delivered to a store near to us, which would be in Lincolnshire, possibly Nottinghamshire. We asked him if the store was open due to Lockdown and he said, unequivocally YES. (spoiler alert, all carphone warehouse stores are currently closed.)

Ten minutes later my partner received around 13 emails, not an exaggeration, some saying the phone would be delivered to our home address, some saying it would be delivered to Newark, some saying it would be delivered to London.

We rang the customer services back, spoke to the call centre who passed us through to sales, spoke to another lad cand regaled the above story. He pressed some buttons and told us the phone would be delivered to our home address by DPD the next working day. At this point, we were so happy the saga had come to an end.

The next day we received an email from DPD saying it would be delivered......the next day.

The next, next day we received an email from DPD at 9am saying the order had failed because no one answered the door - which was odd because we had both been awake and in the house since 7am. We checked the order details and it turns out they had tried to deliver it to...........one of Carphone Warehouse's London stores.

So again, we ring customer services, pass security, they fob us off saying we need to ring DPD, we ask to speak to sales, get through to sales, tell the story, give the lad the order number for DPD, he searches it.....twice...and says that DPD is saying it's not a valid order number and no such order exists. We ask if we can simply cancel the order and get our £50.01p refunded, he agrees and explains we will need to be transferred to customer services because sales can't do this.

We are placed on a brief hold, after which point, an automated message thanks us for calling, and asks us to complete a brief customer satisfaction survey, before hanging up on us.

We call back to customer services, to be told that their systems are down and we need to call back in a couple of hours.

We immediately call right back, get through to customer services, who tell us that they are able to cancel orders and we need to go back to sales, who thankfully, promised a refund within 3 - 5 working days and sent an email to confirm.

Carphone Warehouse, you are an actual joke, your company is trying to cling to existence like Trump is trying to cling to his presidency, I think it's about time you called it a day. I would write a formal complaint, but to be honest, It's just not worth it for the £20 ex gratia apology you will probably give me if I shout loud enough, at this point, I just want every potential future customer to know how awful your company is, and to avoid you at all costs.

We recently applied to renew our mortgage and were shocked to be turned down on the basis of "poor credit rating".

After paying for an Experian credit check, it turned out someone had opened an account in my Husband's name with Shell energy, at a property we don't live in. Shell had been asking for payment, but as we don't live there we didn't receive any bills.

We have spent HOURS on the phone to various customer service agents trying to find out how we can get the account number so that we can discuss the bill with someone.

The third agent we managed to speak to finally understood the situation and agreed to email us a bill so we would have an account number to discuss the issue.

Several more hours and several more customer service agents over the next few weeks insisted they couldn't help us, or saying they would send us an email to reply to with evidence of where we live, only to not send the email.

Finally, I managed to force an agent to stay on the line whilst I waited for him to send the email, refusing to hang up until it was in my inbox. It took over 45 minutes of discussion and being put on hold for him to send one email.

This whole debacle is costing us thousands, as we are now out of our fixed mortgage period, and can't apply for a new one until the credit rating is sorted, so we now pay £700/month more than we had previously agreed with the mortgage lender.

Shell have said it will take 6-8 weeks on their end to get the credit accounts department to remove the listing against our name, but don't worry, they "definitely did" raise a task asking for that to be done (I'm sceptical, based on how many emails they "definitely sent" but never did until I held an agent hostage on the line for nearly 2 hours).

Once their accounts team finally do manage to remove that listing, Experian has informed us it will take 6-8 weeks to reflect on our credit rating.

So *if* the agent actually did raise the task (big *if*) then we could still be 16 weeks, four months, away from being able to apply for another mortgage, which takes about 12 weeks to process.

That means, that since attempting to arrange our remortgage in June, in September we are still seven months away from being able to get one, thanks to Shell.

Overall, this will cost me £4900 (7x£700), not including the number of hours of work my husband and I have missed waiting on hold for their customer service agents, or our phone bills for that time.

I ordered broadband on 15 April 2021, go live date was 30 April 2021.

On my go live date, no one contacted me and I waited for the broadband to work, fair enough. On 1 May 2021 there was no internet. I phoned to find out what the issue was, the gentleman on the phone said, not to worry it would go live today and he would personally phone me back. I heard nothing and when I logged online it now said the 4 May. I would have appreciated a call back to confirm this and not being reassured it would definitely be in on 1 May. Anyway.

The engineer came out on 4 May, phoned me and told me there were no available ports. This seemed strange, as the previous tenants had Sky internet. I phoned Now Broadband and communicated this issue to them (surely Now and Openreach should have some sort of open dialogues between them, and why was I the middle man).

I was advised they would take a look and that this would be escalated and could take 72 hours (what would have happened if I didn’t phone?). I heard nothing further.

At 17:41pm on Wednesday 5 May I received a text message advising Now had tried to contact me – I had no calls. I need received a text message saying an engineer would be attending the next day 6 May, at “anytime”. I work full time and had to attend the office on 6 May, so I tried to phone Now to get an idea of what time the visit would be, after several calls I was advised it was a morning slot.

On 6 May, the Openreach engineer asked me to turn my router on (it was already on from my original go live date), I believe (and again no one confirmed this with me) that the telephone line was working. I was hopeful it might still be fixed as my Nowbroadband page still said I was to go live on 6 May so I waited.

Surprise! On 7 May, there was no internet again, no correspondence from Now or Openreach and the website continued to say good news, you’re due to go live on 6 May (Now had now managed to master time travel apparently)! I phoned Now (again no one at Now seems to be able to call anyone or update anyone). The lady on the phone advised that she would escalate the issue (was this not what was done on 5 May?) and again it could take 72 hours.

I asked to speak to a manager and was told they don’t have phones (interesting), I then filed a formal complaint in the hopes someone would take a look at what was actually going on.

Anyway, a new engineer visit was arranged for 11 May. I stayed home to wait for the hopeful return of internet, so I could successfully work from home again. The openreach engineer arrived and advised he had been asked to look at the phoneline, but there was no issue with the phoneline and that the issue was the fibre connection in the cabinet. He advised there were no notes on the system but that Now and Openreach were discussing the issue and I should hopefully have it resolved by the end of the week.

So I phoned Now again and explained what the engineer had said to me. Now said this was news to them, and it would have to be escalated again – and could take a minimum of 72 hours. So, what had been going on since I was told there were no Ports on 4 May? Why was Openreach and Now looking at the phone line and not the actual fibre connection? I mean, it’s all a bit of mystery to me and apparently an even bigger mystery to the customer services team at Now.

In summary - By the time that’s escalated (even though Openreach assured me it was in hand already), it’s likely I will have lost another week of internet. Do Openreach and Now communicate via smoke signals? If so, can I get involved to try and figure out what is actually going on

So to anyone who is thinking about going with Now, do yourself a favour, pay a bit more and go with someone who can actually provide the service.

So A couple of things with Argos... I don't want to name stores because I think this is an Argos issue as a company. I want to start with my first big purchase at Argos in West of Scotland a few years ago with the iPhone X... Now this is important - Last one in stock** got it, all good. 2 months later the battery started draining rapidly seemingly for no reason. A visit to 2 Apple stores in Glasgow left me feeling bitter as they said they couldn't do anything, but it came across as "I don't believe you" with the aim to avoid costing the company another £800 or so and they just wanted to get rid of me from their busy stores as anything less than "perfection" wouldn't be tolerated infront of customers. Anyway... luckily I fix phones as a hobby, so I investigate to discover that the motherboard was faulty, got my hands on another, replaced it, and it was all fixed...

Now fast forward to recently where I bought a watch, my second time purchasing an item **last one in stock** at a different Argos store in Central Scotland, I picked it up, went to my car, discovered that one of the seals (tape) was opened. I thought nothing of it, perhaps they did a quality check before giving it to me? Nope, I opened it to find that the strap was not tucked it to the buckle, the plastic wrapping was somewhat loose, and one of the hands had fallen off!! Came back to ask for an exchange, nope as it was the last one in stock! Offered to deliver a new one to the same store, I thought no chance, I'm going to buy another one from a different store. Guess what, this one was NOT "the last one in stock" and was an absolutely perfect watch!! Sealed, unopened, strap tucked in, plastic wrapping tight and overall well packaged and put together, unlike the other one which was **last one in stock**.

I really am wondering if they receive returns for faulty items, in the case of the iPhone, give a temporary fix, or not in the case of the watch, and they keep them until it's **the final one in stock** only to get rid of them, hoping the customer wouldn't notice?

I really believe the above. Here's the facts. 2 out of 2 times I've bought final stock items from Argos, and both times faulty. One iPhone X costing £800 with a faulty motherboard, and a watch costing £60 with a missing hand and packaging concerns that scream

"I've been opened, used, returned, not fixed, *poorly repackaged* and sold on"

My advice from my experience is be aware of items that only have 1 stock left. Whatever it may be. Likely chance is that it is faulty, or a returned item as faulty, kept for a sorry someone to purchase last hoping they won't notice.

The silver lining. Sort of...
- Manage to fix my iPhone X myself.
- the watch had to be refunded as there was no more stock available in that specific store. The refund I was told would take **3 - 5 working days** I thought, I'm £60 out of pocket? And essentially double if I want to purchase another that same day? I had faith in that time estimate, even though I didn't get any proof like an email or text to say that I was going to be refunded, so I did buy another from a different store.

To be fair. I got my refund on the Friday after the hassle I experienced on Wednesday, as promised.

Something I don't read often enough, or ever, when I go through these reviews, looking for some peace in mind regarding my refund time estimate, anxiety and worry regarding whether or not I would ever see my refund ever was my concerns after all these reviews.

To anyone reading and wondering about the anxiety inducing, "they were quick to take my money, but take their time paying me back (up to 7 +-2 days for bank card according to reviews, and 30 days for PayPal)"

I have been refunded as promised! and although the **staff member who handed me the watch, saw me, actively avoided me, and looked at a colleague** (ha! thought I didn't notice!) who then subsequently served me, Anyway that colleague was absolutely brilliant, took the item back, tried to fix the problem, refunded me etc.

Again, avoid last items in stock, not worth the risk.
