Like many of the other reviews on here I have fallen foul of the 'trade-in scam' .....yes 'scam' is not overstating the carphone warehouse scheme.....I was quoted £105 for my s8+ and £100 promotion bonus - total £205...Great - what could go wrong?

Bought a new s21+ for full payment as agreed and immediately received an email confirming trade-in as £105 with no mention of the £100 promotion payment. Sent email asking for clarification of my confirmed offer but received no response. Sent another email but still no response.

Sent my used s8+ in the pre-paid package which was in mint condition with no scratches, dings and in excellent working order......remember the criteria at offer stage was it should be simply working, no visible damage or water damage.....after a week received an offer of £25 with a long list of other technical criteria that had to be met and a summary note saying they found screen burn - which is an absolute fabrication as there was NO screen burn whatsoever on my handset sent and it was in perfect screen condition.

I rejected this pathetic offer and requested return of handset - still awaited.

No response to any emails from 'TradeUpHelp at dixonscarphone dot com' (it might be better named No-reply at....) and still no promotion offer payment (customer services on the online chat advised this would be paid with 2-3 days of receiving the handset from me) I have that confirmed in the chat history yet still no payment received at time of this review.

The whole process is to get you to buy the new phone at full price - pay up front on a vague valuation promise that is never (if ever?) fulfilled with a derisory trade in offer on completely different criteria to that made at the original offer stage at checkout.

I would avoid the whole CPW 'trade-in scheme' and just sell your existing handset on online yourself.....that way you will get true value and avoid all hassle of dealing with CPW.

Edit... Update...

So I was contacted by 'Jim' (who you will see below all the reviews here) apologising but in essence offering nothing positive other than to ADVISE me I would not now be receiving the promotional £100 either as that was dependent on me accepting their trade in offer regardless! - THAT was not made clear at the point of offer or at the checkout prior to purchase.....and there are many here on this review site blissfully unaware they will NEVER receive the promotion payment....

So now the scam has been fulfilled with not one penny of the £205 deal being paid (or will ever be paid) AND they still have my perfectly working handset with no clarification when or if it will ever be returned.....

So there you have it - the complete scam revealed.

DO NOT USE this utterly misleading and frankly disgraceful trade in scheme.

I have now written off the so called £205 payments promised by CPW - and most probably won't see my handset ever again!

So my £950 new handset that was meant to include £205 with trade in discount ( ie £745 with discount) has actually cost me £1,100 when you factor in the cost of my handset.

If my handset does ever turn up - and undamaged by CPW I will provide a further update.

Absolutely disgusting service, appalling customer service and inexistent continuity in client care. I am making this publication hoping that I will prevent other people experiencing the pain and time waste I have been put through. Even though it’s almost traumatic for me to go through this timeline of events:
My partner first signed up for Virgin Fibre Broadband services in October 2022. We were told we had to wait about a month until the installation could be done – during that month we contacted Virgin twice to make sure that the cable/ pre-installation work had been done as we knew the area surrounding the house was owned by a property management company and suspected a permit must be needed. Each time we were reassured the external work had been done and there was no expected delay for the engineer visit and installation of services on the 2/11/22. On that day, the engineer said he could not install the services as the external work hadn’t been done. This was then the beginning of countless hours on the phone to try to understand what the problem was.
We then got an email out of the blue saying “I am sorry to hear you have cancelled our services”. We called Virgin to see why we received that and they said they could not explain it (shocker) – in their records we had cancelled it (but couldn’t say how and there were no records of it (!!). We then had to sign up all over again, with the sales team questioning the prices and not honouring the original offer. We asked them to go back on the record and listen to the original phone call but they seemed unable to do this – again not being able to offer any continuity.
After that, I stayed on hold for hours and transferred to the wrong people more times than I can count. I would try to have any sort of continuity by remembering the people’s names to then be told I was speaking to a different call centre altogether or the previous person had made no notes. I was reassured by Virgin that the visit would be done “that day” so many tinmes – I waited days at home, not leaving, afraid I would miss the visit. Again, so much time wasted. The next day the pain of being on the phone again without getting any answers.
The lack of communication between the subcontractors who do the external work and Virgin is ridiculous – I kept being told they had no way of speaking to them! I assumed the delay was due to a permit problem (even though on the phone I was reassured countless times it wasn’t) so I contacted the property management company myself, asked them to sign a Wayleave and sent it to Virgin.
Finally, I am contacted by Kelly who explained that the pre-installation team had been going to the wrong address all this time! Hence the cable work not been done yet. Even though we now knew the problem, they still could not tell me when the cable work would be done. I had to chase it again multiple times when then I am told they now needed a permit from the council. Days go by again and eventually they tell me the permit was for the 19/11/22 and then the engineer visit would be done on the 26/11/22. You have guessed right: not the external work nor the engineer visit happened AGAIN! Virgin sent us a dongle after we spent hours and hours on the phone but that did not even work properly as our house has very poor signal (hence we needing the fibre installed).
This has caused an immense inconvenience in our personal and work lives. It's now 6/12/22 and when I called Virgin today I got the usual “we have a note on our system saying the work will be done today” – a sentence I have heard over 10 times in the past month! We STILL DO NOT HAVE INTERNET (it’s been over a month). This is an absolute joke.
To make it all even better, when we claimed the compensation we are entitled to according to the website “£5.25 per day if we don’t install your services on the promised day until installation is complete” they have also said no and given us a £26.24 cheque instead. Seems fair, right?
Please learn from this experience, and use a company with minimum dedication to costumer service instead.

Two hours later, I received an automated email from carphonewarehouse.com customer services. It simply stated my order had been cancelled due to an "internal security check failure". There was no reason given, no name, no contact number, and no apology. Basically, screw you and your custom.

To get things straight, I live in a house that I own. I am registered on the Electoral Roll. I have a bank account in my name. I have worked and paid tax every day for the last 20 years. To say I was annoyed at the impersonal nature of this rudely-worded, automated, one-line e-mail was an huge understatement.

In disbelief, I rang carphonewarehouse.com customer services. After being on hold for 5+ minutes, I spoke to a gentleman who looked at my order. He was completely baffled and could not give any reason or idea as to why my order had "failed security checks". He volunteered to try placing the order again, but I refused. As a customer, I should not be begging a company to take my money, regardless of product exclusivity... this is the height of capitalistic, corporate greed. Instead, I told the gentleman I was frustrated, annoyed and disappointed, and I would be leaving a review on Trust Pilot. His immediate response? "Don't do that, sir. Don't go onto Trust Pilot". He encouraged me to use Facebook instead and to directly message the carphonewarehouse.com customer services team. This obviously doesn't affect their public ratings and my complaint cannot be viewed by other prospective customers.

So, here's my review. I tried to spend nearly £500 with you and you made me feel like I was trying to commit a crime. When I asked for an explanation, you refused to give one. When I complained, you tried to hush me up. I've spoken to Oppo's customer services team, and asked them to forward details of this instance to their public relations department, because as an emerging international brand, this is EXACTLY the sort of corporate behaviour they need to avoid.

To sum things up, I REALLY want the new Oppo "Reno 2" phone, but as the UK's only stockist of the SIM-free model, I refuse to beg the carphonewarehouse.com team to take my custom. I'd rather go elsewhere, and I'm now considering spending £800 on the P30 Pro with Amazon. Good work, guys.

After 10 days in Slovakia, PC was STILL NOT shipped and I had to leave to Greece. I contacted them again and asked if they could ship it to Greece. I transferred them my address and then waited to arrive in Greece before notifying them they could send the parcel. I arrive in Greece, call to notify that it’s possible to ship; I am told they will proceed with this. 10 days later, no news. I decide to contact them again, and they tell me that actually the order was not shipped because they JUST REALIZED they do not ship everywhere in Greece – and my address was not valid for the shipment.

I get offered to receive the shipment without a palet (for a >5000 euro PC? No thank you). The other option, which I chose, is to pay an extra 250 for shipping with a palet. I asked for a gesture from their part, as the information on their website concerning Greece and the information I was given about shipping to Greece on the phone was false - they refused because ‘they are already refunding me the French taxes’ (note: keep in mind I actually end up paying the Greek taxes which are higher!). At this point, I just need the computer to meet work deadlines, so I pay.

The shipment is sent mid-march with an arrival date on the 26th. On the 26th of March, the parcel does not arrive so I phone customer service which tell me it is actually the 26th of APRIL. But of course, when being offered the 250 euro delivery, they carefully omitted the fact that the delivery did not take ~a week like their regular delivery, but a month and a half! So, here I am waiting patiently until the arrival date. But unfortunately, the day before arrival I get notified that the PARCEL WAS DESTROYED and that the DELIVERY TO THE ADRESS WAS CANCELLED.

So over 4 months – no computer, wasted hours on the phone, days waiting for a delivery that never arrived and lost work contracts.
I know that this order has been extremely confusing – but this confusion would never have happened if they had simply met the shipment deadlines I was given for France AND then Slovakia.

I'm not talking about not being able to get a stable WiFi connection in the attic or the basement, but in the same room, sitting feet from the router. My Brilliant Broadband has given me nothing except a sore behind because I am limited to using Internet only through an ethernet connection, sat on the floor beside the router. I've contacted NowTV about my issue, explaining my issue with not being able to get a WiFi signal from their hub and their response to me was that NowTV "do not guarantee a wireless signal in the home only coming from the line to the hub". This response was followed up with an estimate of the penalty fee I would incur should I chose to move to an ISP that will allow me to use my own router or supply me with one that is capable of a WiFi connection. So, NowTV will supply you with equipment, and restrict you to only using that equipment, but will not guarantee that that equipment will allow you to get a WiFi signal in the same room. My advise to anyone considering choosing nowtv as their ISP is DON'T DO IT!

The BT agent I spoke to responded by saying I was terminating my 24-month contract early for which a charge of about £220 would be made.

I remonstrated with the agent that people could not be expected to live in a place for an exact multiple of two years in order to suit BT, and I had already been responsible for the line for several years (though technically there had been a “renewal” in Summer 2021). I reminded him that I was also a customer of BT elsewhere, having a line to my house in Scotland, so I wasn’t forsaking the company. Indeed, as I further reminded him, I had been a BT customer for many, many years. None of these arguments seemed to make much headway, though he did say he would consult a supervisor. Putting me on hold he returned to the phone a little later to tell me the supervisor confirmed what I had already been told, though as a concession BT would remit one month’s direct debit payment in respect of my line in Scotland.

Subsequently:-
I received an e-mail indicating that I had ordered a cessation from 14th November. (I don’t recall ordering any such distant date.)
I telephoned BT on the evening of 20th October about 5.30 p.m. (20 minutes wait for an answer) to say that I was already removed from the flat and could they please cease their service immediately? The lady responded by agreeing a cessation the following day, 21st October.
Late on 21st October, one of those “Don’t reply to this” e-mails arrived from BT to say there was a change to the order and the cessation would in fact be 14th November.
More than three weeks after my original call, on 8th November, BT took a further £44 monthly direct debit for the Cumbria line; this was three weeks after a new owner had moved in!
Only quite recently have I received my final bill for the line from BT, showing a cessation date of 18th November (not 14th as their e-mails had indicated) and calculating a final net “payment due” of £203, which money they have now taken. So, since my original call, a total of over £247 has been taken from my account for the Cumbria line.
I have not received the indicated one-month’s remission from BT in respect of my continuing Scotland line; indeed, BT have just e-mailed to say they are about to take a further direct-debit for that.

In September 2023, this remaining BT line, which by then I will have held for nearly ten years, will reach the end of an exact 24-month period. At that time, I would hope to cease my foolish brand loyalty and find some other broadband provider. There are several – and some will surely show me better standards of customer care and loyalty than I have experienced with BT?

There was a time, back in the day, whereby if you wanted to see a bunch of clowns performing then you paid good money and went to the nearest travelling circus.

Today, you just order something from ao, open a bag of popcorn, sit back and watch their "logistics" operation fail miserably.

We paid £55 for a five hour delivery slot, in our case 12p.m - 5p.m. That way, our morning wouldn't be disrupted and the evening would be free to visit my seriously ill mum in hospital. By the way, £55 isn't a typo - yes, ao *really* do charge £55 for a "reserved" time slot that they have no intention of honouring; they don't prioritise your delivery, for example, their route planning software simply generates a fuel-efficient delivery route for the driver to follow. If that happens to mean you're drop 40 out of 40 for the day then you're looking at a 10p.m delivery, regardless of the "reserved" time slot you've paid for.

Now some might say that £55 is a large (even extortionate) fee for merely sticking a finger in the air and announcing which third of the day they'll pretend to deliver your item.

I wonder what percentage of "reserved" time slots are actually achieved and, more importantly, whether ao refund the charge when they fail? I'll bet a pound to a penny that they try to hide behind terms and conditions and only refund when faced with a small claims action. Hmmm, I feel a data access request coming on.

Anyway, our delivery journey started off badly, tailed off in the middle and the less said about the end the better. We logged onto their tracking website to see where our delivery was and at 12.10p.m it said there were 29 drops ahead of us. As the afternoon went on, the delivery time slipped further and further back. Now bear in mind we'd paid £55 for a 12p.m - 5p.m slot, by 4.50p.m they were already advising us that there were 13 drops still ahead of us and that delivery would be between 7.00.pm and 10.00p.m!

So that's the visit to my seriously ill mum in hospital down the Swanee.

At 7.40p.m we took a call from someone at their logistics department who said that the crew had bailed out due to "a family emergency" and so there would be no delivery....although at this point they were already almost 8 hours past the start date of our "reserved" time slot so I don't believe that there was any way they'd have managed a delivery before midnight.

Thankfully I am not a BT customer. But I am looking to change broadband providers and was considering BT. BT appear to only do 24 month broadband packages.
After speaking to the online chat advisor I asked if the service ended up being poor which is what is described in some of the other reviews and someone wanted to leave prior to the end of the 24 month contract what would be the early termination fee.

Her response was:
If you cancel your contract before 24 months then the months left in the contract multiplied by Monthly package price - VAT. Then further 1% minus from this figure to give total charge. will be your your cancellation charge.


Example calculation: Your monthly BT Plan is £30 a month. If you cancel with 6 months remaining, we multiply the £30 by six, totalling £180.
UK VAT (20%) is taken off off that figure, leaving it at £144. Finally, we take 1% off that figure, making your final Early Termination Charges £142.56.Early Termination Charge (ETC) calculation: (Monthly Rate X Months remaining) - VAT. Then further 1% minus from this figure to give total charge.

Therefore I wanted to post this so others can be aware, rather than going with BT on a whim that it might be okay.

By the time I am writting this my order has been stuck in pre-production for 23 working days while percentages of orders dispatched in the last 5 days (for Desktop computers) are the following:

- 7 Days: 16.28%
- 14 Days: 73.28%
- 21 days: 94.99%
- 28 days: 98.12%

I understand PCSpecialist works on a queue system and sometimes there are out of stock components that take time to arrive. That is perfectly understandable given the state of the market. In order to make the process as smooth as possible I think opening a channel of honest communication with the customer is key. This is not what I found.

Since I ordered there have been a few red flags that make me feel uneasy:
- After the order was stuck in pre-production for 2 weeks (they advertise < 1 week on their website) I decided to contact PCSpecialst to check if there were any problems with the order. Only then I was told there was a problem with the stock of the cooler that I requested and that if I replace it "this should allow your system to move forward through our production stage". The other coolers available were more expensive so I ended up spending 40£ extra.
- After I few days I asked if everything was ok as the order was still in pre-production. I was answered that's how the queue system work and that I have to wait but should be going into production by the end of the week.
- Fast forward to the following week I get a new email asking me to change another component (the case) because it is out of stock so they can proceed "without any further delays" as they are planning to place my order as "priority". Again I pay more money for the amendment but I ask if there is anything else holding my order and they answer that there isn't.

My order is still sitting in pre-production and when I wrote again for a follow up the answer has been silence. An additional note is that the cooler that I had to upgrade to allow my order to go to production should now be back on stock.

Definitely not the experience I was hoping for.

Edit (from 1 to 2 stars): I have now received my new computer and so far everything is working as expected. The process was fast once it reached to production. The build is clean and the components were properly installed. If it wasn't for all the previous experiences with the process and the situation being a mishandled I would probably would give it a much higher score. Probably giving customer services the ability to mend the situation and compensate the customer when this happens (maybe with a free upgrade cover up to x£) would help to tackle the situation better.

Ok so I moved here from Canada and needed a cheap and easy SIM/number while I get settled in.

Found Three standing out to me in a Tesco and just got it, I wasn't complaining I just needed a way to make calls in the UK until I could get a contract with a mobile provider and pay as you go was the cheap and easy solution. Inserted the SIM, topped up, easy enough.

When I tried creating an account for easier top-up/account management I suspected that I made a typo in my email because a) I wasn't receiving the activation mail and b) after exhausting the manual "send me a mail" button attempts I just got a generic error saying something was wrong.

Contacted chat support. And this is where it gets fun.

Told support that I was trying to create an account with Three and that I was not receiving an activation mail. Got connected with a support tech and after 20 minutes of the tech asking me to clear cookies and such on my laptop to log in - despite me explaining to the tech at least twice that the problem was not receiving the activation mail because I did not have an actual account, they finally understood and transferred me to another tech in another department that would help.

Round 2.

I connect with the tech and they catch up on the chat. They make me do a couple of things such as clear cookies and such again despite me explaining again that I just don't have an account and the issue is that I'm not receiving the activation mail to create my account. The tech notices that there's an email mismatch (yay!) and after some security checks changes my email. I then receive an email from Three that the tech sent with a link to log in that could give me the option to change passwords and such.

Now, keep this email in mind. It becomes important.

So the tech asks me to try to log in now and I tell them I'm still getting an error. Long story short, after asking once or twice if I should just just click the link in the email on my laptop to change my password, I had been asked to:
- Clear cookies and browser history on my laptop (again)
- Log in and try on my mobile device
- Download "the app" which ended up being a waste of about 20 minutes because there was a pay-as-you-go specific app that I was supposed to download instead but never asked to download it specifically
- Try logging into the pay as you go app
- Clear cookies and browsing data on my mobile device
- Provide the iOS version and phone make/model
- Turn off wi-fi/VPN and ensure I was connected to the Three network

And a few other things that were too exhaustive for me to remember

All these attempts did absolutely nothing and the tech insisted to follow their instructions despite the link sitting in my mail.

Anyway.

After almost 45 minutes with this tech (well over an hour in total at this point) I was frustrated and accidentally navigated away from the chat window while trying to follow one of their instructions on my laptop instead of my phone. I got disconnected. And at this point there was no way I was going through this whole ordeal again, so I went back to my email and clicked the link in the mail that was sent to me towards the beginning of the 2nd round of troubleshooting.

Guess what?

It worked.

I was taken to the Three account creation/login page, clicked login, went through the prompts and when available I clicked on "reset password". And. It. WORKED.

While I appreciate the techs needing to stick to a script, over an hour of unnecessary troubleshooting could have been done in less than 5 minutes if I would have just been asked to click on the original link that was sent to me for the sake of password reset purposes.

The network does what I need it to and hasn't failed me, but troubleshooting my issues was a painful experience with was seemed to be inexperienced staff that either didn't understand my problem or were strictly following a script - plus I still can't log into any of the mobile apps. Not a huge loss though since I can still access my account and top-up on my laptop.

Also I can't add any international minutes to my current package (they're just...not available?), but I'm not reaching out to support to figure out why. I'd rather deal with swapping SIMs and roaming charges with my Canadian provider until I get a contract with another provider.

But yeah. It's a cheap mobile network and it does the job for what I need it for. It's just their tech support that is severely lacking.

I am not like most people who will just rate 1 star because of 1 small issue. So I am gonna break this down with how much you get for your money and is it worth it?
Now TV is quite expensive when you compare it to the other services like Prime and Netflix. The only thing worth buying is Sky Cinema and Boost for HD streaming (Which we all know we shouldn't have to pay for in this day an age) and more devices to watch simultaneously. I live on my own so I feel like I am being charged for something I will never use. You can also buy live sports if you are into that which is good as this is the only way to watch premium sports live afaik unless of course TV subscriptions like Sky and BT.
With The Entertainment pack you get several TV channels to watch (Non Freeview) which is alright but I think it should give you the option to rewind back to the start of each show if you started watching halfway through. Also it says it adds 300 plus channels which aren't on Freeview. This isn't exactly true. You get around 10 live channels and the rest is just shows from other TV channels. Rather then charing people for more shows you should combine them into Now TV and then have a Live TV pack that offers a bundle of Sky Channels to watch Live. Another stupid thing is No pausing on Live channels. This is absolutely unreal. There is no reason you cant use storage cache on someones PC to pause. This makes the TV channels pointless imo. You can get Freeview plus which has no subscription price and you can pause and record (Only Freeview channels ofc). So if you pay for the Sky Cinema and Sky Entertainment and Boost your talking £25 which is the price of Netflix and Prime put together.
Another huge let down to this service is the regular 30 second adverts that have no skip option. I get annoyed when amazon does this with a skip option because you're charging people for a service and then forcing everyone to watch adverts. I am debating whether this company even cares about the feedback its getting because it doesn't seem to do anything about the issues people are not liking. When searching on Google at films it doesn't even advertise if it's on Now TV when its been around for longer then Netflix and Prime video. This service has so much potential as the GUI (Graphic User Interface) is fluent and works well. Better then amazons. To watch anything you do have to download the player which these days is ridiculous. It also has no buffering so if your internet is bad then you won't get HD which you would be getting charged for. They should ditch this player and just have it for live TV and then allow people to watch in browser with buffering to make sure everyone can get access to HD. There is no issue with the player itself as it does work completely fine. But in this day and age where browsers are so advanced there is no reason to still use this method of streaming. If NowTV made a few updates on fixing the problems I have listed, added some more content and also funded some exclusive shows. Advertised its exclusive range it could become as big as the other services but until that happens its gonna remain unused by a majority of the community. I mean seriously most people haven't even heard of it.

To summarise my review.
Allow people to skip adverts.
Only have player for live TV and ad a browser play that includes buffering to ensure everyone has the ability to stream HD as slower broadband won't be able to do this with the current set up.
Combine the Entertainment and the Cinema packages and then have live channels separate. If this is profitable anyway which it most likely is. Charging the same price as Prime and Netflix for entertainment and cinema packages just seems way to much imo.

Only thing worth paying for is cinema and boost imo.

This service does have the potential to compete with amazon and prime but the question is will the development team be able to listen to feedback and work on improving the service for the paying customer?

Edit: The Mac OS player doesn't work at all. Constantly gets an error saying about screen recording. Review dropped to 2 stars.

Then to the issues with their customer service..

Importantly, during these conversations, I specifically asked about the need to return the router, as I was relocating abroad in a few days and had to know where to send it to. This turned out to be a mistake, as almost a month and a half after I cancelled my contract, I received a letter asking me to send the router back, with a threat of a £50 penalty if not returned! All in all, very ineffective customer service with reps giving out wrong information and failing to resolve your request or to follow up. Contract cancellation made unnecessarily difficult: I had to contact them by chat and phone three times before they managed to cancel my contract. Fourth time to deal with the router scenario. And now, apparently I will have to contact them for a fifth (!) time in order for them to remove my details off their mailing list /right to be forgotten! I was told it was too early to do this during today’s chat.

TalkTalk: pay more to your call centre staff in order to hire and retain quality people. Train your management to spot situations where wrong information is given out.

And lastly, why on earth was my bill put up by £10 suddenly in the last couple of months? To top things off, when I cancelled my contract before moving out, I was told I’d need to pay another full month while they ‘disconnect’ my service.. So £36 for a month I did not use the service. A nice way to treat a loyal customer eh?

The man was trying to be helpful but did also tell me, "well anyone can post any number on the internet". This company is leaving people open to receiving nuisance calls by allowing their users to enter any mobile number they want. After the man said anyone can post anyone's number up without any checks, I will be writing to the ICO to report their negligent handling of personal data. I did not give permission for my number to be shared with numerous companies and added to marketing lists and they should not have facilitated it.

Bark.com needs to ensure that verification codes must be entered before a mobile number can be used and shared via their website.

Message to Bark.com

I am posting this review to raise awareness of the importance of GDPR. People have a right to keep their personal data secure and not to receive numerous marketing calls they did not ask for.

If you had asked me three months ago what I thought of PC Specialist (PCS), I would have raved about how delighted I was with my 15.6” Defiance Laptop. What a difference a few months makes.

I bought my laptop from PCS four years ago on the advice of a knowledgeable friend and decided to go high end to get something that would last and cope with my demands as a professional programmer. Although it’s essentially a gaming laptop, I don’t really use it for games.

I’ve been very happy and productive with it up until September when one of the fans started to roar like a diesel engine. I called PCS but after four years, it was out of warranty and they no longer stocked the fan in question, but was told that if I took the back off, I could identify the fan and maybe obtain a 3rd party replacement. However, despite being very careful, when I replaced the back, the laptop had completely died!

I called PCS again and they assured me they’d collect it and repair it, including the fan. However, when they’d received the laptop, I was told that the motherboard needed to be replaced and it would cost nearly £800. I was gobsmacked. The PC was only four years old and had cost over £2,000. I was also told that the warranty for the repair would be limited and that the fan could *not* be repaired - even though it may have caused the problem in the first place. When I asked what was wrong with the motherboard, I was told simply that the technician had no idea.

I was advised to buy a new laptop and told that I could transfer some of the working components across. However, even that became problematic when firstly I was told that I’d need to get a new copy of W10 Pro even though I already had a license and secondly, when I asked if PCS could offer any good will gesture discount given the short life of my expensive laptop, I was told that wasn’t possible.

Even so, I agreed a spec and waited for the order to be placed. After a week, I called again check progress and, despite being previously told I could move the SSDs and the 32Gb DDR4 RAM to the new PC, I was *now* told that putting older parts into a new PC wasn’t company policy so in effect I would have to completely junk my laptop and buy another.

At this point, in frustration, I asked them just to send it back to me. I’m *so* glad I did as I then spoke to a local guy who arranged an inspection and repair by an independent lab in London. All that was wrong was that a simple voltage regulator on the motherboard needed replaced. The guy even fitted a new fan. All this for a fraction of the cost of what PCS would have charged me for a new PC, which turned out to be completely unnecessary anyway. My laptop is back and working as well as ever.

PCS make great computers, but my impression of them has been badly tarnished by lackluster and inconsistent customer service. My laptop was with PCS for over a month and every time I spoke to them, the story was different. I lost faith that they had any ability, or motivation, to repair my laptop. They just seemed to want to sell me a new one.

I won’t forget this experience and despite being happy with my laptop, I’m not sure I’ll be shopping with PCS for my next PC or laptop. My advice to others with a PCS product that's out of warranty would be to find somewhere more competent to diagnose and hopefully fix the fault.

I have been using Ebuyer for about ten years just for myself alone;

However, with one of my latest orders, a graphics card was faulty. Unfortunately, I was unaware of this to start with, and by the time I was, it was past the 30 days for a replacement to be sent out.

I was told it could take up to two weeks for Ebuyer's repair teams to fix things, and if they can't, it would be sent back to the manufacturers for repair and can take up to 28 days for it to be repaired and sent back.

This totals 42 days.

I have had to wait over 50 days to get anywhere, with me having to continually phone up to get information about what is happening.

The ONLY update I got on the return ticket was three days AFTER I had gotten the information after one of the phone calls I had made. I was told during the call that the graphics card would have to be sent to the manufacturers as they could not fix it onsite. This was 21 days after it had been sent to them, and I was told they had known this about a week before I had called. With the return ticket update, came a tracking number that only logged that the item was sent the next day, nearly two weeks after they were aware they could not fix it onsite.

On the 18th of this month, I was told (after phoning up after having waited for the call they said they would give me) that the card was apparently sent back to them from the manufacturer on the 1st, 18 days before the call.

They have decided that instead of making me wait any longer, they will send me a new card in replacement and apologise for the delay and trouble I have faced. That is it.

However, instead of sending it then and there, I had another four days to wait as they sent it on Monday.

In addition, the next day delivery was delayed because the delivery diver, who only delivered 15 out of their 99 parcels that day before calling it quits. As a result, I wasted a day waiting on a graphics card as the tracking information only updated after 8 pm that night that the delivery would be coming the next day. This was not directly Ebuyers fault; however, I am told I can only log a complaint through Ebuyer and with how poorly they have handled this return, I don't see that any complaint I log will have anything done about it unless I call Ebuyer up every day.

I have lost nearly two months of computer use, a computer I need for my work. It would have cost me less to have paid for a new card than the loss I've had with the delay on the card.

I am genuinely disappointed in the entire handling of this return. From the lack of information, the non-existent call or emails they told me I would get from them by the next day (I only ever got any information after having to spend more time calling up to find out the answers myself, sometimes a few days after I was meant to get a call or email.), the amount of time this had taken and the fact that I am now supposed to be happy with the new card being sent to me, no compassion for the delay, no (empty) promises to find out why this has taken so long and to let me know what has happened, nothing, not even an email saying we are very sorry that this has happened.

I have never had such a terrible problem with a NEW product or a company that I have been a loyal patron of for years. While the people I talked to were very polite and sympathetic, the company's response and actions were beyond disgraceful.

I am still determining if I will ever use Ebuyer in the future. However, I will no longer recommend it to friends, family and, most significantly, not to my customers.

About three years ago, I replaced the primary drive, a 2 TB HD, with a Samsung SSD 860 EVO 250GB, purchased from Mr Memory. The 2 TB drive was retained for extra internal storage. The Samsung SSD worked fine, and my HP PC continued to give good service. However, in hindsight, 250 GB was not large enough for the ‘C’ drive, which recently filled up after installing Apple iCloud (which appears nowadays to only install on the ‘C’ drive of a PC).

To keep my HP PC in service for another few years (hopefully five or more), I recently replaced the 250 GB Samsung SSD with a Kingston 2 TB, KC600 SSD, using an SSD upgrade kit that included a download coupon for Acronis cloning software. I purchased the upgrade kit from Mr Memory.

However, cloning with the Acronis software didn’t work for me. All the extra space of the new SSD was added to the HP_RECOVERY (D:) partition, which then showed 1.62 TB free of 1.63 TB. That wasn’t much use, as I need the extra space on the ‘C’ drive partition. I struggled for hours with the Acronis cloning software, trying to adjust the size of the four partitions on the primary drive, but it always failed to allocate any extra space to the ‘C’ drive, and it remained stuck at 206.77 GB.

In the end, I found a couple of very useful YouTube videos titled ‘Old PC Upgrade #2: SSD Boot Drive’ and 'Drive Cloning & Imaging' by Christopher Barnatt of ExplainingComputers. That alerted me to Macrium Reflect cloning software, which I downloaded for free.

The Macrium Reflect software was a dream to use compared to the Acronis cloning software. It worked perfectly and allowed me to resize the four partitions on the primary SSD to my requirements and increase the size of the 'C' Drive to 1.82 TB.

If anyone is struggling with Acronis cloning software, I would strongly advise them to use Macrium Reflect.

I had no problem with the service from Mr Memory. It was fast and efficient. But perhaps they should recommend Macrium Reflect as an alternative to the Acronis cloning software.

I was looking to build a PC, but with the not-so-recent graphics card supply issues, it's made it harder to do so. I will admit, I did look at more companies other than just PC Specialist, comparing costs and delivery time - as well as base cost if I were to buy all the parts myself.

In the end, PC Specialist seemed like the best choice. I looked at a few reviews and they were pretty positive. I think it's important to do your due diligence before spending a decent chunk of money and they were very transparent with where to find their reviews. Always a good sign.

I will admit, I purchased a few days before December so was a bit unsure if I would receive before Christmas. Come to the delivery, DPD were great. Knew when to expect it, and the delivery guys were very kind as to leave it where I requested.

The setup of the PC itself was incredibly simple. Just had to remove a protective foam within the PC and plug everything in. It all worked first time. I did have a few beeps and, upon my own research, just had to reseat the memory and GFX card - both of which I was able to do myself. I may have knocked them while removing the foam so just something to be aware of.

The PC has been running fine since, with "fine" being an understatement. It's great and I love it. Definitely made a few friends jealous!

Another thing to quickly note is that your order arrives with a box containing the relevant manuals (and stickers!) for certain parts (like the motherboard). Pretty useful. Also a little handbook from PC Specialist themselves which was appreciated.

All-in-all, I would recommend buying from PC Specialist. May even do so myself in the future.

Despite the negative press the company has (perhaps deservedly) received, I can only write from my own experiences which have been surprisingly positive. After an Openreach line fault and years of a substandard ADSL2+ connection, I looked at the old Telewest faceplate in the living room and, thanks to the option of a 1-month rolling contract, decided to give Virgin Media a try.

The QuickStart package was delivered on time and after getting connected, the line was active with minimal fuss. I started out on M300 and the bandwidth was as promised, which was - at the time - a revelatory experience, as my previous connection was just 10Mbit down/1Mbit up via ADSL2+. Surprisingly, latencies were also good; despite the inherent jitter of DOCSIS technologies, my average ping had even reduced by a few ms. Note however that I put the Hub 3 into modem mode and used my own router: an ASUS RT-AX82U. I cannot in good conscience recommend any VM customer to use the Hub itself as the router.

Unlike friends I had known to use Virgin services, there was no peak time congestion, no packet loss or skyrocketing pings. Just a steady, consistent service. I suppose I won the postcode lottery? The experience convinced me to sign up for an 18-month M500 contract, and the bandwidth increase was carried out as promised without issue. I have been with them for nearly 2 years and can count the number of times I needed support on one hand - in these instances, the forums were more useful than strictly via phone.

I have to dock a star for a couple of reasons - there was a period of several months where the connection would be down for hours at a time, or drop out and reconnect at an awkward moment. However it has now been stable for a few months with no sign of further issues. Also, in order to get the best contract deals, which seem to be largely arbitrary and not published on the website, you have to threaten to cancel and go through the retentions team.

When my contract period expires I will be moving to another company, because multiple FTTP altnets are overbuilding in the area and the technology is simply superior (until VM themselves eventually finish their XGS-PON upgrades). However if this isn't an option in your area, you can do worse than taking a chance on VM. Just take up a one month contract, and see how they do for a few months before negotiating any longer-term commitments.

I recently installed BT's unbreakable wifi Halo package.
BT's home tech expert is supposed to:
1. Make sure your broadband connection is perfectly set up for you and your home. The home Tech removed my old router and connected the new one.
2. If you've got Complete Wi-Fi, they’ll set it up, giving you guaranteed wi-fi in every room. BT's policy is to only send out one wifi disc with the router. THerefore, if you need 3 discs The Home Tech Expert cannot do their job properly. There is a tool on the My BT app to check the signal strength, but the Home Tech Expert didn't use it. The signal strength checker lacks discrimination as a measurement system because it only measures 4 levels. Measuring signal strength with an app you can get on your phone gives the measurement in dBm and this can give precise information when the signal starts to drop and where the discs need to be placed. Therefore, I don't understand why BT have this policy of only sending one disc out at a time when it can be determined, up front, how many discs are needed.
3. Explain your security features and parental controls, helping protect you and your family. The Home Tech Expert made no attempt to do this.
4. Answer all your tech questions and show you how to use the My BT app. The Home Tech Expert made no attempt to do this.
When I showed the Home Tech Expert the email from BT detailing what he was supposed to do I got no response. When I wrote a complaint email to BT, they closed the complaint without providing details of why they had closed it. When I phoned them up to find out what had been done they told me they had contacted the supplier to inform them of the complaint. No feedback was ever obtained.

When the new Halo service was installed it was very unstable and the lights on the router indicated a problem with the service. These problems had always been there, but were not as bad with the old router. In fairness to BT they did send out two Openreach engineers. The first engineer fixed two line faults, which reduced the faults but did not eliminate them. The second engineer fixed another line fault which the first engineer did not detect. I question why the first engineer did not detect all the faults. A simple ping test revealed timed out errors, and unstable connection on video calls is an indication there could still be line issues on the service providers side. Aren't BT supposed to monitor line drops. In fairness to BT I now have a system that works, but I would not rely on BT to fix any issues in the future because K don't value their customer service or technical service. One final observation : Before the second Openreach engineer visited and found the remaining line fault, a clear line test indicated there were no line issues!!!!!!!!!!!!!!

Purpose of this review is to describe my dealings with PCSpecialist customer service department, this is not the review of the actual computer, for which I'm still waiting ( 50 odd days). I just wanted to provide some feedback to anyone who thinks about buying new pc from PCS in these difficult times.

PCSpecialst probably was one of the best custom PC manufacturers in the country before Covid pandemic, sadly this is not the case anymore.

I have bought 3 machines from them in the past and they all work fine thus I have decided to purchase from them once again, the decision which I have come to regret.

I know that market is in really difficult spot now so before the purchase I gave PCS a call in order to discuss my concerns and components availability. After short conversation I have ordered new pc with graphics card that I was told was in good supply. Estimate build and delivery time I received was 16 to 19 working days which was quite promising. This was never kept. While I was waiting for my pc to be assembled I noticed that some of the pieces I have picked were now showing as out of stock on their website. I have contacted customer service to ask them about this and I was reassured that delays won't affect me if component I picked didn't show as out of stock at a time of placing the order. After waiting another week or so I have contacted them again and this time I was told that unfortunately GPU I have ordered is out of stock and my order is going to be delayed. I was also told they expect a delivery soon but nobody knows when and how many units will arrive. Great...

I have waited yet another 2 weeks but my order was still showing as '' pre production''. I have checked PCS own forum and I have found a post regarding assembly time and I noticed that people who ordered just few days before me, have already received their computers while I was still in the queue. I have contacted PCS via chat and I was told that they have some great news for me and that my pc will be built within next few days, which actually turned out to be 2 weeks, so much for the great news...

My pc have finally reached building and testing stage which took roughly 1 day. I thought that end of my misery was near but PCS decided to not let go of my pc that easily. It sat awaiting to be dispatched for 3 days. I have contacted them on Thursday and I was told that my pc would be dispatched the following day and I would get it on Monday or I can pay 20 quid extra for Saturday delivery. I agreed for Saturday delivery however my pc has still not been dispatched. I have spoken to one of their agents on late Friday afternoon and he said that the orders have already been collected and unfortunately my pc didn't make the cut, despite me paying extra for Saturday delivery. I was told there is a backlog of orders which has to be cleared before I receive my machine.

I have finally lost my patience and decided to rate my experience before I even had a chance to lay my hands on the computer. Honestly speaking I think even 1 star is too generous for what I have been through.

Don't get me wrong, I'm not a spiteful person. I work in customer service industry myself. I fully understand online retailers woes ( Covid outbreak, staff shortages, driver shortages, global issues with GPUs supply and other) however I would expect a little bit of honesty and professionalism from the company of this calibre.

I can understand many things but lying to your customers I cannot. I was told 16 to 19 working days (about a month) while in reality I'm waiting almost 2 months and have to constantly chase for updates myself. Nobody EVER got in touch with me to let me know my order has been delayed. To make things worse, info I have received from various PCS agents more often than not, turned out to be false. All this despite spending almost 3 grand on a computer I really need. Not good enough.

Lying to your customers is UN-AC-CEPT-ABLE.

A good friend of mine who bought a pc from a different retailer in the middle of covid outbreak was told upfront he would have to wait 3 months for his pc but he was updated throughout the process and the delivery time he was initially given was kept to the day. That's why I don't buy this ''we don't know when, we don't how many'' excuse PCS seem to love so much.

If other businesses manage to do it, so should you. It's very clear that whatever business model PCS has, it ain't working anymore. Time to regroup and get your act together. You make millions selling computers yet you can't even provide acceptable levels of customer service. Stop feeding BS to your customers.

After previously purchasing a customized laptop from PCS 6 years ago, I decided to use them again for a replacement laptop.

I configured a 17.3" Ionico laptop & placed the order at a total cost of £1930.

The order was placed on 19th January & I received the laptop on 8th February.

After powering on, initially nothing appeared on the screen & the keyboard went into "disco" mode (multi-coloured flashing). The laptop sometimes tried to start Windows but said it had detected errors & was unable to repair the PC. Most of the time, it was in cyclic reboot.

2 different technicians attempted to recover the PC but finally agreed it was likely to be a HW fault.

An RMA was raised & the laptop was collected the following day.

Late afternoon (Friday), I received an update from an RMA tech confirming that they had the same issue as reported & they would build a new laptop with new components. The following Tuesday, I received notification that my new laptop was built, fully tested & ready for dispatch. I received it on Wednesday afternoon.

This time, the laptop started Windows but it was for user Administrator & that user account was disabled. As such, I was unable to use the PC & I contacted tech support again. It was necessary to perform a clean reinstallation of Windows. However, MS 365 Personal (a 12-month subscription via digital license) was not working correctly. No account activation was recognised for my MS account. The support tech told me that he would sort this but because he was not in the office on Thursday, I agreed to wait until Friday & he would call me to continue. That never happened & I had to call on Friday afternoon to chase it up. Another support tech attempted to fix the problem but then found out that the problem was that the digital key was not bound to the new laptop HW so he would arrange for that to be done & call me back to continue. No response was received (call or email) so I called again late afternoon only to be told the relevant people were not available & nothing could be done until Monday.

On Monday, I called & was told that they needed to speak with the licensing department as to how this can be resolved. After a while, I received an email stating that the only options were "either refund me for the payment made for my office package or alternatively they would have to bring my system back under an RMA and have a key installed/injected to my system".

Following the guidelines on the PCS website, I raised a formal complaint via email & also arranged for my laptop to be returned under a second RMA as was suggested by PCS. I specified on the RMA that I did not want the laptop returning to me until I had received the result of my formal complaint. It was collected the following day & delivered to PCS the day after (Wednesday).

On Friday, I called PCS to find out why I had not received any acknowledgement of my formal complaint (website states "When we receive your complaint we will acknowledge this by email to the account registered on our site"). I was told that my case was under investigation by a complaint's manager. I asked to speak to a manager but was told that was not possible, so I asked for an update (either a call or email) to be made before the end of the day. Nothing was received.

This whole experience is unacceptable. From day 1, I have spoken with at least 6 different support techs. Each one has made verbal assurances about contacting me (callback and/or email) & what they would do to resolve the issues, all of which then never happened. I have had to call & chase this up every time & I've had to deal with a different person each time. When I asked to speak to a specific support tech, it has not been possible & always felt coerced into dealing with the person on that phone at that time. My feeling is that the support techs make verbal assurances to placate the Customer but never deliver. This just has the effect of making the Customer feeling let down & being lied to.

From reading current reviews, I am not alone in my experience & it appears that the only time PCS seem bothered & contact the Customer is when somebody leaves a bad review.

I placed the order on 19th January & as of 28th February, I still do not have a fully working laptop as per my order.

To suggest that the initial HW fault could have occurred during transit is debatable but for the other SW-related issues, that should never have happened from such a company.

It is a shame because the previous laptop I purchased from PCS worked fine from day 1 & never had any problems. It's only when things don't work that you see a side of PCS that is somewhat lacking when it comes to Customer satisfaction. Yes, problems do eventually get fixed under the RMA process but when some of those problems are genuine mistakes by PCS, it is not acceptable for PCS to think that the Customer should accept this as being OK.

What a strange experience with AO. We have ordered about 6 appliances form AO over the last 15 years. On Monday 23rd January, we ordered a Samsung 65in OLED TV. I received an email acknowledging it and almost simultaneously an SMS. The email didn't advise of any problems. Assuming the SMS to contain the same confirmation text as the email, I didn't read it in full. It looked like a standard confirmation text.

The next day, we received a shipment notification email complete with tracking link. The TV was apparently on its way. Another SMS was sent in the morning advising of a more precise delivery slot. We suspected nothing wrong. Waited all day, the TV did not arrive. 24 hours later I clicked on the delivery tracking link to find it was not loading details.

I called customer services and was advised that upon ordering, I was sent an SMS asking for a copy of my a statement to go with my credit card to prove I was the owner of the credit card. What on earth is that all about? Never in my 20 years of online shopping have I come across that. From a bank maybe but not a reseller. Its usually my bank's responsibility to check the transaction is not fraudulent. I went through 2-factor authentication to make the payment in the first place.

I checked the SMS mentioned by the young lady from customer services and lo and behold, although it came at the precise moment as the email confirmation, it contained different information. Incredibly bad logic to include an important request like that in an SMS but not in the email! This completely unorthodox request came in the format of what looked like a scam/phishing SMS. I say that because upon reading it I noticed the message was asking me to send my bank statement to a web address, and not an email address! Turns out their SMS server mistranslated the "@" symbol into a "j". So AO's instruction was not even valid.

However, all of this was too late as I did not respond in time. The refund had already been initiated prior to me calling. Why would I suspect any issue when I was getting delivery notification mails and tracking links? After putting down the phone, the same TV jumped by £450. I kid you not. The same TV also jumped price with another big online reseller.

This is the complete truth and AO do not seem the slightest bit interested in improving their processes which have made them look like black market crooks. Of course they will cry the additional checks are for customers safety, I'm not contesting that, I'm contesting the manner in which it was conducted. A phone call would've been wiser. Don't send important information like that by SMS whilst failing to include it in an email. This isn't 1995.

Good by AO. You lost a valuable customer.

I have purchased 4 computers from PC Specialist over the last 11 years and after long and hard thought about the service and product received this time round, it was good overall, but not quite good enough to achieve 4 stars.

Ordering:
Went smoothly, no problems.

Sending in case:
Within half hour of my case being signed for at PCS I had an email confirming they'd received it - Nice for piece of mind.

Build Process:
My order sat in "Processing" for 11 days, then into "pre-production", to "in-building", to "in testing", to in "QC" and to "awaiting dispatch" in the space of one day.

My PC then sat in "Awaiting Dispatch" for 5 days before I received a phone call.

I'd left a note inside the case asking for them to run an extra Sata / Data cable so I could add another SSD.

The phone call was to inform me there wasn't enough SATA headers on the MB for them to run the extra cables and what did I want to do. I was suprised it had taken 5 days post build for them to contact me since I'd been checking for the tracking number each morning.

I told them not to worry about the cables, and instead I'd move my files to an M.2 SSD and install that instead.

Next day I received the PC.

First Impressions of the machine physically:
Greasy marks and dirty fingerprints everywhere didn't look great.
I felt the cable management could have been better, particularly the big bunch of cables connected up right in front of the CPU cooling fan which must impact air flow to some degree. There were other cable routing options available that could have avoided this (I guess those routes were not used as it looks like they might use cable routing as a means to support the GPU during transit)
One of the case side panel thumb screws was only on a couple of threads, but the other one was so tight I had to get the mole grips out.
The PC was supplied without the M.2 stand-offs and fitting screws that would have come with the motherboard, and the process in getting them sent out to me was infuriating - I had to provide evidence they weren't supplied, and it took 9 days from receiving the PC before they finally agreed to send them out (You can buy from amazon for £3-£5 so hardly something I'd lie about)

Impressions of the machine operationally:
The PC booted up and ran very well initially.

It was the noisiest PC I've ever used - it would easily drown out 10 playstation 4's running at full chat, I couldn't hear the door bell over it.
Then I noticed the cooler had been plugged into the AIO pump header which by default has one setting - "Full Power". A quick adjustment to the fan curve in bios and the problem disappeared, but should have been done before dispatch.

One of the front case USB type A ports didn't work, should have been picked up in QC I'd have thought. Turned out the cable was not connected to the motherboard and the way the cables had been routed made it too short to reach. I had to buy a USB Motherboard extension cable to connect it up, and now its working fine.

My front USB type C port doesn't work. I've still not worked out if the port is faulty on the case I bought and sent in, or if they haven't connected something, but regardless I think it should have been at least picked up in QC.

XMP was pre-set in the bios and the 5600Mhz ram is operating at its full capability which is good and something I think that is often missed on pre-built PCs.

CPU Benchmarks (i5-13600k)
Cinebench R23
CPU multicore score of 23995 @ 51C
CPU singlecore score of 1956 @ 53C

At time of testing the average benchmarks for this CPU are 23702 and 2018 respectively, so my machine has overperformed in multi core and under performed in single core.

Geekbench 5
Multicore score of 17128
Singlecore score of 1937
Max temp reached was 70C
Again, from what I understand, average Geekbench 5 scores for my CPU are 15127 and 1960 respectivley, so again my machine has well over performed in multi core and underperformed in single core.

Considering my case is a "Silent" case I guess the max temps were good. The CPU fan didn't go above 35% on the Cinebench, but was indeed maxed out on the Geekbench test.

Conclusion:
Since I already had the case I was going to try building this PC myself. Using the Scan website for every part (to avoid the aggro of shopping around multiple places), the total cost of all parts added up to £1498 including delivery.

Using PCS I got the PC built, delivered and a 3 year silver warranty all in for £1581.

The value in using PCS is certainly there, even though customer service can fall a little short if you get through to the wrong person, and Quality Control leaves a bit to be desired, at least in the case of this PC.

It is also fair to point out my first PC from PC Specialist in 2011/12 (i7-3770) is still going strong with zero issues in 11 years having now achieved over 47000 hours run time and plenty of life still left in it.

All of the telecoms companies have committed to providing social tariff rates for people like me who are in receipt of means tested benefits. BT's version of this is *supposed* to be BT Home Essentials, but they won't tell you about this product, even if you ask. They are more likely to sell you a more EXPENSIVE broadband package than you're already on, which was what happened to me on my first call to them last week to discuss how I could access cheaper broadband. Even if you tell BT EXACTLY what you want, ie "I want BT Home Essentials", they will say they'll put you on that plan but that too will be a lie. Because they won't do what they say, they'll just fob you off with promises and platitudes. When you call again the following week, to chase up your new service, they will tell you that you are not actually in receipt of Income Support (one of their eligibility criteria) even though you are...even though it is your husband's name that receives it through the National Insurance number, and YOU, as his wife, are deemed to be on Income Support for ALL other legal purposes including claiming Housing Benefit or free school meals for your son!!!...they will bizarrely suggest that YOU should instruct the DWP to change THEIR systems...it would be funny if it wasn't so distressing.

I'm disabled with Ehlers Danlos Syndrome, in a wheelchair and I need cheap broadband. I suffer with depression, and extreme anxiety for which I have ongoing counselling. These phone calls to BT have tested my mental resilience to its extreme. I have cried at times which is so embarrassing to admit. My husband is my carer, hence Income Support for Carers (a very specific type of benefit that blows up BTs algorithm) and my husband was diagnosed with stage 4 cancer last February. If we, on our low income and in our vulnerable position, don't qualify for the social tariff then who does???

The attitude of blunt advisers who transferred me through to dead ends, or to others who couldn't help, was particularly challenging as I LOVE repeating myself over...and over...and over...knowing they're never listening to me and that they do not give a damn and that nothing will change because BT simply don't care about providing even a basic level of decent customer service. Special mention must go to Joseph, in the "loyalty team", who offered broadband and basic TV at 39.99 per month. But when I asked if I could take some time to think about it, as I don't want a full 24month contract because - to be blunt - I don't know if my husband will die in the next 24 months, Joseph warned me that I would need to decide there and then. He said, "I can't promise that this offer will be available beyond today". Talk about duress and bad sales practice.

I have had enough of them. I feel discriminated against as a vulnerable disabled customer about whom they don't just not care. They pay lip service (in meaningless policy statements) to their supposedly accessible services!

I have now raised this matter with OFCOM. I will raise it with relevant Members of Parliament and the media (where necessary) in order to raise awareness of how inaccessible & misrepresented BT's supposedly beneficial social tariff truly is. As a former lawyer myself, if I had ever treated any of my clients in such an obstructive and disdainful manner, I would have rightly expected to go out of business.

It's a shame that BT are too big to fail; they certainly don't deserve to succeed. If you have the opportunity to choose your broadband/TV provider, go ANYWHERE other than BT.

This is the third review I have had to write for TalkTalk in the space of just over a month, each time the customer experience has become worse than last, which I never thought possible. This latest incident is, however, the most serious since it now places the health of a 92 year old customer at risk, and yet TalkTalk continue to make excuses and deny that complaints have been logged on their system, despite assurances to the contrary from the staff to whom I have spoken.

After trying to fix a fault on my father's landline for weeks, with no assistance from TalkTalk, this latest incident has occurred today on his discharge from hospital. The Ambulance service who took him home tested his Careline unit as part of their duty of care, only to find that the unit could not connect due to the fault on the line. To make matters worse, this has tied up the line meaning that my father is unable to make and receive calls, something which is very important as our only means of contact with him at present. If this had been a genuine emergency instead of a test of the line then the consequences could have been disastrous.

Since my father's phone line isn't working and he has no internet I have been trying to speak to TalkTalk's technical team for over an hour now, having been cut off 3 times. Each time I am asked the same questions, to which they already know the answer, the most important of which is that a health alarm unit is attached to the phone line (something of which TalkTalk are aware since they confirmed this in an email to my father yesterday).

My experience with TalkTalk has been reported to Ofcom as this cannot be an isolated incident and it is disgraceful that a telecommunications company with a duty of care to its customers can place the health and wellbeing of vulnerable customers at risk simply because it will not take responsibility for faults or respond to customer complaints.

I am only too well aware that there will be a stock response from TalkTalk noting that they are very sorry that this experience hasn't met their high standards (which are a joke) and asking me to provide more information so that they can look into the matter. Other than making them appear to be concerned, this will have absolutely no value as once the information is provided they will yet again lapse into their state of denial, refusing to fix the problem or to follow their own procedures in dealing with the complaints that they so conveniently mislay.

It is about time that the telecoms industry was given a regulator with teeth who could pull the licences from businesses such as this.

UPDATE ON 5 OCTOBER:

An Openreach engineer attended my father's home this morning, and the contrast between the service provided by Openreach and that provided by TalkTalk couldn't be starker. The Openreach engineer was polite and helpful, taking time to identify the fault and replacing what he believed to be the part causing the fault and then verifying that the line was working correctly. Not only did he fix the fault, but he called me to advise me that my father's line was now working, and even took the time to set up the broadband router that we have had no end of difficulties obtaining from TalkTalk.

I stand by my original rating of TalkTalk, particular now it has been demonstrated how a professional telecommunications company (Openreach) can behave. TalkTalk are an absolute disgrace and should have their licence revoked for endangering the welfare of vulnerable customers and lying to try to cover up their failings.

I bought my new gaming PC through PCSpecialist rather than build it myself. I know that PCSpecialist will do a great job with the build quality (including wiring) and their PCs last years (my previous PC was a PCSpecialist PC built way back in 2009!).

I had to wait a little while but when it was finally dispatched it came the next day, well packaged with everything as I expected. I turned it on and noticed the fans were running at 100% - the noise was very noticeable. It seems that PCS saw fit to put their logo on the case and on the MOBO screen at start up, but do nothing with the fan profiles themselves. Fortunately, this didn't cause much inconvenience to me - I had a friend come around to help replace the stock case fans and put in 2 extra ones, and she changed the BIOS fan settings to something that made much more sense - now the fans run idle and only spin up when the temperatures rise - and even with the extra fans, it is MUCH quieter, especially when not playing intensive games - but to someone not knowledgeable about PCs, they would literally be sitting there with the PC sounding like a jet fighter about to take off, all the time, with no respite. That doesn't make sense to me. Also, they had connected the AIO cooler to the wrong socket on the motherboard, meaning the BIOS wasn't reading the fan speeds correctly. Simple testing (by starting the PC and looking at the first screen in the BIOS settings) would have shown them this.

Overall I'm very happy with the PC, and they did a good wiring job, and I know PCS builds last a long time, so I'm giving them 4 stars. But I'm withholding that extra 5th star because if I was not an enthusiast user, I wouldn't have known about the fan speed issues, and I'm sure there's a lot of other PCS customers sitting there with really noisy PCs for no reason.

Sometimes it pays to be mindful of the rules, guidelines and regulations that apply to the service you are buying. Sadly, there are also a bewildering number of laws and regulations that can be extended to cover broadband, mobile and or phone “services”, such as the Consumer Credit Act or Consumer Contracts Regulations (distance Selling Regulations). Please have a look at (ISPREVIEW DOT CO DOT UK) for details as to how some of the relevant rules apply.

The rules and guidelines of the Advertising Standard Authority also apply and are implied terms of your contract with the internet services provider. Accordingly, you must bear in mind that low speed, for example, is an automatic breach of contract by the provider which entitles you to seek to bring any long term contract to an end without any penalty to you. Particularly, where the company is in breach of contract, they must put you in the same position as if there was no breach on your part with you not have to make any further payment or continue to use the company products. A further example, lets say you had a 24 months contract with “dot internet”, but dot internet failed to provide the promised speed. You contact the company in writing retaining proof of communications. But dot internet ignored and or the low speed continues without improvements. That would be a clear breach of contract by dot internet entitling you to terminate the contract and bring it to an end. The company’s debt to you, to say the least, would be the payments due for the remainder of months you would have had to pay the company had they not breached the contract of service.

To recap VM are implementing price rises of retail price index(R.P.I.) + 5.9% every year. The R.P.I. is NOT considered an official inflation rate by the Government. They use Consumer price index(C.P.I.). BT, EE and most other companies use the CPI as a basis. CPI is currently 10.5%, whilst RPI is 13.4%

Both measures attempt to measure the effect of prices on a typical household and do NOT reflect the effect of inflation on VM's costs.

On top of the inflated inflation rate VM are adding 3.9% and will be doing this EVERY year.

If VM choose to reply to this review then please justify:
1. Why use RPI
2. Why increase this by 3.9%
3. Why insist on this every year.

I switched from Virgin to Cityfibre due to assurances that it’s reliable from

Then they said there was some sort of “gap” in the cabling further up the street to the cabinet, so it couldn’t be finished. No idea what the issue was, but whatever. It took Cityfibre until yesterday, Friday 7th October, to send an engineer out to blow the cable. I was promised that it would be arranged “within the next 10 days”, which seems mean “we’ll bother to call you to arrange the visit exactly 10 days from now, then the visit will be at some point after that”. That seemed to work, and the lights on the ONT are all green.

But the internet is STILL not connected. The Internet light on the router is flashing red indicating it cannot be authenticated at Vodafone’s end. It was doing this all day yesterday. I wasted an hour on the phone to be told “everything is done our end, it can go live any time until midnight” even though it was patently obvious it would not magically fix itself at 2 minutes to midnight.

Quelle surprise, it doesn’t work this morning either. I have wasted another hour on the phone to Vodafone, only to be told that it is something Cityfibre need to fix, and they may need an engineer visit. But they’re shut on weekends, so I need to wait until Monday

I have been 12 days without broadband, relying on the 4G backup dongle. I have had to waste HOURS on the phone to both Cityfibre and Vodafone to find out what’s going on. And now it will be 14 complete days without broadband, assuming they actually fix it on Monday, which is seeming increasingly unlikely. No doubt I’ll be waiting another 10 days from Monday for the Cityfibre engineers to bother looking at the appointment system and scheduling me in. I am not even convinced it’s Cityfibre’s issue here, as the connection test the guy did to the ONT yesterday worked, it’s just the Vodafone authentication that’s not working. It’s definitely not the cable or the router hardware, as I’ve tested my own router (with the correct PPPoE credentials I was provided by Vodafone) and other cables.

I asked Vodafone to just try resetting the PPPoE credentials, as based on other forum posts, this seems to be the solution. They flat out refused and said “the problem is with Cityfibre”. This would fix the issue within minutes, but they’re unwilling to even *try*. This constant buck passing and refusal of both sides to accept any responsibility is absolutely ridiculous.

Don’t bother upgrading to Cityfibre through Vodafone if you get a circular through your door promising fast speeds, it’s probably not going to work and they’re not going to expend any effort whatsoever trying to fix it promptly. When it does eventually connect, I’m fully not expecting to get remotely close to the advertised speeds.
